385YE Winter Solstice Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for Astolat, Bregasland, Hercynia, Kallavesa, Miekarova, Necropolis, Ossium, Skarsind, Temeschwar, Weirwater and Zenith. The Senate named Vesna Borkovna Prochnost to the Throne and appointed ambassadors, the Imperial Administrator, seven generals and many sinecure holders. The Synod elected cardinals including Darian Numbers of Prosperity and Ashborn Atla of the Way, plus inquisitors and champions. Seven Military Council strategoi were appointed. Archmage candidacies were declared for Night and Summer. Bourse auctions sold the Weirwater Vales, Golden Trees of Seren and other seats, while the Chair of the Wolf (1055 votes) and Reeve of Boar's Market (867 votes) were among the Bourse elections.

n.Dawn: Dawn returned Bohemond De Rondell for Astolat and Ser Lucan Mortére for Weirwater, and Mouse of Dawn was appointed Strategos of Dawn.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Senate appointed Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra as the Empire's Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highguard returned Eli of the Cenotaph as Senator for Necropolis, and Seretia was appointed Strategos of Highguard.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind, the territory the Imperial Orcs held at the time.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; they are linked only as holders of Bregasland, for which Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold was returned as senator.
n.Navarr: Navarr returned Rowyn of the Waystone Path as Senator for Hercynia, and Edric Lonestrider was appointed Strategos of Navarr.
n.The League: The League returned Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar as Senator for Temeschwar and Gabrieli was appointed Strategos of the League, while Valentina von Temeshwar became Master of the Sword Academy of Temeschwar.
n.Urizen: Urizen returned Herminius of the House of the Wanderer as Senator for Zenith.
n.Varushka: Varushka returned Troyan Dobrociech for Miekarova and Marya Zoranova Doubek for Ossium, and Doubravka Nadjaovna Vanek-Vessely was appointed Strategos of Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark returned Rane Shardbearer as Senator for Kallavesa, Vidarr Rune-Bound was appointed Strategos of Wintermark, and Nora was named Grimnir of Wittal Grove.

t.Astolat: Bohemond De Rondell was elected Senator for Astolat.
t.Bregasland: Lizzie Stamp of Bildewold was elected Senator for Bregasland, though the territory was held by the Jotun at the time.
t.Hercynia: Rowyn of the Waystone Path was elected Senator for Hercynia.
t.Kallavesa: Rane Shardbearer was elected Senator for Kallavesa, and the Senate appointed Nora as Grimnir of Wittal Grove within the territory.
t.Miekarova: Troyan Dobrociech was elected Senator for Miekarova.
t.Necropolis: Eli of the Cenotaph was elected Senator for Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Marya Zoranova Doubek was elected Senator for Ossium.
t.Skarsind: Bloodcrow Rasp was elected Senator for Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Giuseppe Sanguineo von Temeschwar was elected Senator for Temeschwar, and Valentina von Temeshwar was appointed Master of the Sword Academy of Temeschwar.
t.Weirwater: Ser Lucan Mortére was elected Senator for Weirwater, and the Weirwater Vales seat was won at Bourse auction by Misha Kemi for 440 thrones.
t.Zenith: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer was elected Senator for Zenith.

r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Senate appointed Nora as Grimnir of Wittal Grove.

385YE Winter Solstice Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 601 thrones and 4 crowns. The Senate criminalised the Last Resort poisons and Ocean's Caress, and created the Arcane Inquisitor. An Arcane Envoy also passed, though its appointment method needs correcting. It declared the Rahvin foreigners and recognised Thule dominion over Krevsaty, Miechernya, Crow's Ridge, Silver Peak and the Webwood. Funds went to the Wintermark army (200 thrones), Spider's Dream Bridge (240), Dawn's fourth army (55) and Temeschwar great works (44). Commissions and announcements created counting houses, sinecures, bourse seats, ministries and a spy network in Reinos. Ambassadors were elected to the Grendel, Axos, the Iron Confederacy and the Sarcophan Delves.

n.Dawn: Dawn received 55 thrones for its fourth army and gained the Phoenix Flame in Astolat and a Counting House in Semmerholm, and Bridget Talbot de Couerdefer was elected Imperial Administrator. The Rahvin of the Barrens were declared foreigners.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Senate elected Finna i Fijadoz i Guerra of the Brass Coast as Ambassador to the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highguard's senators secured the criminalisation of Ocean's Caress and a Counting House in Reikos creating the Benefactor of High Chalcis. The Senator for Necropolis received 240 thrones for Spider's Dream Bridge, later amended to drop its fortifications.
n.Imperial Orcs: Human prospectors and miners were welcomed into the northern hills of Skarsind to work the Imperial Orc mines, in a motion fully funded by Irontide Flax.
n.Jotun: The Imperial Spymaster built a spy network in Reinos intended to speed the closure of the Jotun war and hamstring the Lasambrians on the western front.
n.Navarr: Navarri citizens were elected Captain of the Senate Guard (Arthur Bannerman) and Ambassador to Axos (Fintan Nighthaven), and Bledri and Siân of the Eternal Family pledged 10 wains to the House of Illumination. A proposed Leviathan's Hall in Miaren failed.
n.The Brass Coast: The Keeper of the Breadbasket halved the armies of the Brass Coast's losses from insufficient supply, and Brass Coast citizens were elected Ambassadors to the Grendel and the Iron Confederacy.
n.The League: The League gained a raft of works: Holberg's walls, Garden City, souvenir stall and weirwood bourse seat, Tassato's Counting House and Office of the Lantern Wolf, and 44 thrones for Temeschwar great works. Its Legacy mana was redirected to Spiral's spires.
n.The Marches: Marcher senators carried the creation of the Arcane Inquisitor and an amendment letting the Legion Engineer build and upgrade fortifications. A historical report on the Ore Hills Rebellion of 326YE was also commissioned.
n.Thule: The Senate recognised Thule dominion over Krevsaty, Miechernya, Crow's Ridge, Silver Peak and the Webwood as part of Otkodov, pledging not to challenge it while bound by the peace it seeks to extend, and the Thule will be informed.
n.Urizen: The Warmage is to be appointed by the Urizen generals, pending further scrutiny. Urizen gained the Gloaming Forum in Morrow, the House of Illumination in Redoubt, a larger Brilliant Star mithril output and A Fair Price in Zenith.
n.Varushka: Varushkan senators won recognition of Thule dominion, and Karsk gained the Leshun Market and an improved Bursar of the Conclave ministry, with a Light Market in Miekarova. Motions on Semmerlak drowning and outlawing privateering failed.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark received 200 thrones to complete its army and gained the Hall of Rund in Kallavesa, and Thanmir Hrafnar was elected Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves. Research into a vision of Wintermark's Last King, Alof Bearing, was commissioned.

t.Astolat: The Phoenix Flame sinecure and the title of Tender of the Phoenix Flame are to be built in Astolat, to be ceded to Meraud once constructed. Its senator also received 55 thrones for the fourth Dawnish army.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion's senator seconded the Ocean's Caress ban and proposed the election of the Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy.
t.Bregasland: A proposed appraisal into using the Otterway military road to better Bregasland and ease its disgruntled mood was withdrawn.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's senator proposed criminalising Ocean's Caress and seconded the Reikos Counting House.
t.Hahnmark: The Senator for Hahnmark received 200 thrones to complete the Wintermark army begun in Winter 384YE, in a motion prioritised by the Conscience of the Senate.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia's senator proposed the Arcane Envoy title and seconded the Ambassador to Axos election.
t.Holberg: Holberg's walls gain a deep embankment, and the city is to become the City of Flowers, with a souvenir stall sinecure and a weirwood bourse seat. Its Legacy of Courage mana will now go to Spiral.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman's senator proposed the Ambassador to the Grendel election and seconded the Hall of Rund.
t.Kallavesa: The Hall of Rund, a liao-giving sinecure held by the Speaker of the Crows, is to be built in Rundhal, Kallavesa.
t.Karov: Karov's senator proposed making drowning in the Semmerlak the default execution in Karov and other territories, but the motion failed.
t.Karsk: The Leshun Market ministry is to be built in Karsk, and the Bursar of the Conclave's ministry was improved there. A proposal to make Semmerlak drowning the default execution in Karsk failed.
t.Miaren: Miaren's senator secured an appraisal of using fleets to disrupt enemy operations in the Bay of Catazar, but a proposed Leviathan's Hall in Miaren failed.
t.Miekarova: The Light Market is to be built in Essk in Miekarova, with a Merchant Boyar title, though its senator's motion to outlaw privateering on the Bay of Catazar failed.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold's senator proposed the Arcane Inquisitor title and seconded the withdrawn Otterway appraisal.
t.Morrow: The Gloaming Forum, a weirwood-purchasing bourse seat assigned as an Urizen national position, is to be built in Operus, Morrow.
t.Mournwold: A historical report on the Ore Hills Rebellion of 326YE was commissioned, and Mournwold's senator seconded the Legion Engineer amendment.
t.Necropolis: The Senator for Necropolis received 240 thrones to construct Spider's Dream Bridge; the planned white granite fortifications were later removed.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Ossium was among the territories named in the failed Semmerlak execution motion, and its senator proposed the Axos ambassador election.
t.Redoubt: The Brilliant Star mithril bourse seat's output rose to 28 wains a season for higher upkeep, and the House of Illumination is to be built in Cargo.
t.Reikos: A Counting House sinecure, funded by Highguard benefactors, is to be built in Reikos, creating the Benefactor of High Chalcis to oversee its herb gardens.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's senator proposed the appraisal of the Dry Patrician problem in Madruga and seconded Spider's Dream Bridge.
t.Semmerholm: A Prosperous Counting House folly is to be built in Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's senator proposed removing Spider's Dream's fortifications and seconded the Wintermark army funds.
t.Skarsind: Prospectors and human miners will come to the northern hills of Skarsind to work the Imperial Orc mines.
t.Spiral: The League Legacies will supply mana to Spiral's spires, cutting the Senate's seasonal cost from 35 to 5 thrones, though an appraisal of Urizen–League cooperation in Spiral failed.
t.Tassato: Tassato gains a Counting House folly and the Office of the Lantern Wolf sinecure, and its Legacy of Ambition mana now goes to Spiral.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's senator received 44 thrones for tax-providing great works, and its Legacy of Loyalty mana now goes to Spiral.
t.The Barrens: The Rahvin sept in the fangs of the Saltmarsh region were declared foreigners, protected by Imperial law.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin's senator seconded the League mana motion and proposed the Sarcophan Delves ambassador election.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's senator proposed the Legion Engineer amendment and seconded the withdrawn A Fair Price motion.
t.Volodmartz: Mentioned in passing: Volodmartz's senator proposed recognising Thule dominion and seconded the failed Leviathan's Hall.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater was named in the failed Semmerlak execution motion, and its senator proposed the Phoenix Flame.
t.Zenith: A Fair Price, a farm sinecure for the Champion of Prosperity, is to be built in Iteri, and Zenith's senator carried the Warmage amendment.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes souvenir stall sinecure was established in Holmauer Park, completing its restoration.
r.Karsk/Moresvah: The improved ministry of the Bursar of the Conclave, allowing crystal mana purchases at standard cost, is to be constructed in Moresvah.
r.Morrow/Operus: The Gloaming Forum bourse seat is to be built in Operus.
r.Mournwold/Ore Hills: A historical report on the Ore Hills Rebellion of 326YE, its leaders and their fate is due by the Spring Equinox 386YE.
r.Zenith/Iteri: The A Fair Price farm sinecure is to be built in Iteri, though a Senate motion is needed to give the Champion of Prosperity custody of it.

385YE Winter Solstice Synod judgements.d: Enacted mandates sent missionaries to Asavea's hidden sects, scattered Urizen's sword scholars across the Empire, created the Imperial Orc Bone Pilgrimage, set Freeborn corsairs to escort shipping on the Bay of Catazar, and committed the League and Dawn to the Grand Inspiration of the Way. Highborn and Varushkan armies gained new orders against Cold Sun. Many statements condemned cruelty in the Barrens and the Iron Helms, and urged help for Brass Coast refugees. Ozren de Orzel was recognised as an Exemplar of Pride. The Senator for Sarvos and Doyen Ioseph were revoked, and the virtue fund closed the summit almost empty at 3 rings.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish assembly backed a new Knight Protector of Day against Cold Sun, praised its fleet captains and the Free Folk who joined the nation, challenged its senators and generals over the Barrens, and enacted a mandate committing Dawn to help build the Grand Inspiration of the Way.
n.Druj: The Varushkan assembly declared it time to destroy the Druj, announcing a new army that would light torches at Ratibor's Gate before marching to end their threat; elsewhere priests asked whether the Empire's conduct in the Barrens was any better than the Druj's.
n.Grendel: The Grendel were the target of several judgements on the Bay of Catazar: the enacted Freeborn mandate removed the penalty they imposed on Imperial fleets, while Navarr and Dawn urged their fleets to strike at them and their Asavean allies. The Shuttered Lantern was also asked to investigate alleged contact between Spiral's Urizeni and the Grendel.
n.Highguard: Highborn mandates let all Highguard armies use the Bring Virtue to the Scions and Defence of the Virtuous orders, and urged support for the Imperial Orc Bone Pilgrimage. The assembly condemned the Iron Helms, offered Peerless Kinship to the Marches and announced new Casinean Games, but a call to raise a Grey Guard army was withdrawn.
n.Imperial Orcs: A General Assembly mandate created the Bone Pilgrimage adventure for Imperial Orcs to bring ancestral bones home to Skarsind, and their own mandate claimed authority over questions of orc souls on behalf of the Mournwold orcs. Their priests pledged a year of liao at 1 ring to the Freeborn, and their assembly spoke out for the Rahvin.
n.Jotun: The Freeborn assembly urged the Empire to let the Jotun raise a statue to Avisena i Kharizmi i Guerra, which would also free seven thralls to join the Empire; the Jotun were also recalled as past occupiers of Bregasland.
n.Navarr: The Navarr assembly asked the people to consult their guides on the newly found answer to destroying the vallorn, turned its oaths against the Cold Sun, pledged to defend the Great Forest Orcs and urged wayhouses to protect roads and trods. Calls to end tenured titles failed, and Aneira Exile's End became Voice of Barbs.
n.The Brass Coast: With blight spreading from the Blightheart of Madruga, the Freeborn assembly urged citizens to flee and accepted refuge offered by other nations, while all three Freeborn armies marched home. Its enacted mandate set corsairs to escort Imperial shipping on the Bay of Catazar, and it accepted cheap liao from the Imperial Orcs.
n.The League: An enacted League mandate urged citizens to fund the Grand Inspiration of the Way but blocks mandates for other building projects for a year, while a Pride mandate raised congregation income in Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar. The assembly also backed a temple-orphanage in Holberg, removed the Senator for Sarvos and warned of flooding from a curse on the Bay.
n.The Marches: An enacted Marcher mandate pledged to defend the Mournwold orcs against charges of heresy, and another bound the Strong Reeds to Bregasland, giving them extra strength there unless they fail to defend it. The assembly also proposed the Tusks become the Mournwold army and opened an exchange of priests with Urizen.
n.Thule: Navarr thanked the Otkodov scholars who aided the Hacynian research and shared its results with the Thule, while a Varushkan inquisition vindicated the Volodmartz senator's motion over the regions ceded to the Thule, on the basis that it does not recognise their ownership as permanent.
n.Urizen: An enacted Urizen mandate scattered the sword scholars across the Empire, so those at Anvil will be the last of that tradition in Urizen. The assembly offered refuge to Brass Coast refugees, opened Redoubt's Academy of Arms to refugees, sought exploration of returning Spiral to Urizen and revoked Doyen Ioseph.
n.Varushka: An enacted Varushkan mandate let its armies use Bring Virtue to the Scions in Varushkan territories, but bars the assembly from further mandates until Cold Sun is defeated there. Varushka also backed the Imperial Orc Bone Pilgrimage and a new army against the Druj, while the Iron Helms were widely condemned and a move to revoke their general narrowly failed.
n.Wintermark: Two enacted Wintermark mandates urged the nation through a harsh winter: they reward units fighting at home or hunting the Suaq Wastes, and ensure no Sermersuaq settlement goes hungry. Eska Crowspeaker and Yulia Kasimirova Voronov were added to the Chronicle of Heroes, and a bid to strike the magpie as a virtue bird failed.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: a withdrawn Dawnish judgement praised Lady Leysandra de Rondell for seeking a rose from the gardens of the Castle of Thorns, seat of Dawn's kings and queens.
t.Bay of Catazar: The enacted Freeborn mandate set corsairs to escort merchant ships of every nation, removing the Grendel penalty on fleets here. Navarr and Dawnish fleets were urged to fight the Grendel and Asavean warships, and the League warned that a curse to deny enemy fleets the bay would bring significant flooding.
t.Holberg: The League assembly unanimously called for a grand temple-orphanage in Holberg to welcome those displaced by Imperial action, and asked that the new weirwood seat in Misericorde be allocated by League national auction.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman was described as being under emergency conditions and sheltering many Brass Coast refugees, and Urizen asked to recognise Delara i Fijadoz i Guerra as a sword scholar to support refugees.
t.Karov: Threatened by Cold Sun's Blade of Skies, Karov was urged by the Varushkan assembly to aid Imperial armies, and proposals were invited for a hall of fabric arts there. Dawn also called adventurers to end the Deadwood Knight on the Karov–Weirwater border.
t.Madruga: The Dry Patricians' blight spreading from the Blightheart prompted Freeborn calls for Madruga's people to flee, and the Silent Bell was directed to investigate it and its links to the Tutamen family. The Synod also honoured Commonwealth embassy soldiers who died covering the escape of citizens.
t.Morrow: Urizen offered the Temple of the Four Winds in Morrow as shelter and schooling for Brass Coast refugees, and the Prosperity assembly commended the Rising Tide's plans for Morrow, including a ministry selling weirwood for iridescent gloaming.
t.Otkodov: The Navarr assembly thanked the scholars of Otkodov for aiding the Library of Hacynian's research on behalf of the Dragons and welcomed sharing the results with them.
t.Redoubt: The Prelate of Adelmar's Shrine opened the Academy of Arms in Redoubt to all Imperial refugees, a call the Ambition assembly endorsed, and Urizen invited martial sword scholars to debate the Sentinels there.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos sheltered Brass Coast refugees and was warned of flooding from the Bay curse. Its congregations will earn more from art pilgrims under the Pride mandate, and the League revoked its senator for supporting sacrifices to the Semmerlak sovereign.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: listed as one of the places where most Brass Coast refugees are currently sheltering.
t.Skarsind: Under enacted mandates, Imperial Orcs will seek ancestral remains across the Empire and bring them home to the Ossuary Temple in Skarsind on the new Bone Pilgrimage. The Ambition assembly also sought to consecrate a site to Thrace, possibly in Skarsind.
t.Spiral: Urizen warned against appraising Spiral before the Reckoning is settled, asked the Empire to explore returning it to Urizen and invited artists to imagine its future. The Shuttered Lantern was to investigate rumoured contact between Spiral's Urizeni and the Grendel, and the League warned of flooding there.
t.Tassato: Tassato's congregations will earn an extra 36 rings from art pilgrims under the Pride mandate, and it was named the best-returning site for a virtue fund counting house, for which funds were approved.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's congregations gain an extra 36 rings from cultural pilgrims under the Pride mandate. Its exemplar Ratibor inspired a new Varushkan army and a rewarding for those who broke the Vyig, and its former bishop's call to appraise Spiral was opposed.
t.The Barrens: Imperial conduct in the Barrens drew wide condemnation, including the destruction of the Montanians, the threat to the Rahvin in the mithril mines and the position of the Black Wind. Assemblies urged diplomacy, and Dawn called several senators and generals to inquisition over its Barrens strategy.
t.The Semmerlak: The League warned that the sovereign Dho'uala is killing travellers across the Semmerlak, and revoked the Senator for Sarvos for backing a proposal to sacrifice people to it.
t.Volodmartz: With Cold Sun's Shepherds of Ash believed to be assaulting Volodmartz and its trods destroyed, the Varushkan assembly urged people to flee and other vales to take them in. Its senator, Desilav, was inquisited over his motion on the ceded northern regions and vindicated.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Ozren de Orzel's pilgrimage to the Pits of Ennerlund, where he laid unquiet ghosts to rest by hearing their stories, was among the signs that saw him recognised as an Exemplar of Pride.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The League assembly asked that the new weirwood seat in Misericorde, linked to the newly found flaxen pillars, be allocated by League national auction.
r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse will draw larger audiences under the Pride mandate, gaining an extra 108 rings at the Spring Equinox 386YE.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: A bid to recognise Dogri Thulebane, defender of Crow's Keep in Crow's Ridge, as an Exemplar of Loyalty failed for lack of a greater majority. The keep's remnants now lie within a Thule fortification in this region.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Urizen urged the spires of Ossuary to look to their fellows in Ankra on how to pressure the League if it backed appraising Spiral before the Reckoning is settled.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion's spires were named alongside Ankra as the Urizeni that Ossuary should consult on pressing for the Reckoning to be completed faithfully.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Urizen invited the spires of Ossuary to work with Ankra and Cinion to apply pressure if the League supported appraising Spiral early.
r.Temeschwar/Hanuri: Mentioned in passing: Florion von Temeschwar, described as the pride of Hanuri, received a 2-Throne rewarding for helping break the Vyig.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Navarr assembly pledged the nation's fury against anyone who endangers the Great Forest Orcs, who recently recovered their homes in the Heart of Peytaht.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The Varushkan assembly urged the people of Brez to flee the Shepherds of Ash with all speed.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: The vales of Livardz were called on to offer hospitality to Varushkans fleeing the Shepherds of Ash.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: The vales of Opascari were asked to shelter refugees from Marupa and Brez fleeing the Shepherds of Ash.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: The vales of Suvretz were urged to share all that is worthwhile with kin fleeing the Shepherds of Ash.

385YE Winter Solstice interlude.d: Military units could join the Grand Tour tourneys in Dawn. The Guerdon of 350 thrones went to supporters of five armies. Freeborn corsairs could evacuate rebel slaves from Marlien via the Calatropos coast, and Freeborn, Marcher and Winterfolk fleets could hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow from Caitun. The end of the Grendel peace treaty brought raids on southern shipping, while Dho'uala still troubled Semmerlak fleets. Urizen congregations lost authority over the Paragon of Blades. Magistrates disrupted Bregasland, the Icy Maw halved mana in Redoubt and Morrow, and Casinea was cursed. Tharim feasted on Brass Coast resources in exchange for supporting the Fire of the South.

n.Dawn: Dawn's victory celebrations brought the Grand Tour tourneys to Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater, but Dawnish fleets again suffered from the menace of Dho'uala in the Semmerlak.
n.Grendel: With the peace treaty ended, independent Grendel raiders preyed on Imperial shipping along the southern coasts, including around Grendel-held Feroz, for an unknown length of time.
n.Highguard: Highguard felt Grendel raids on its fleets, a Whisper Gallery hunt that cut mana output, and business losses from funding Free Folk priests. Its congregations, however, gained liao, votes and income from the Birthplace of the Way, and Casinea was cursed.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun is not named, though Bregasland, which it held, was disrupted by magistrates sent by the Senate to root out traitors among the households.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn corsairs could rescue Asavean rebel slaves and hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow, and Madruga's Atalaya Harbour made fleet upgrades cheaper. Grendel raids and Tharim's black frost, however, hurt Freeborn fleets, mana sites and vervain harvests.
n.The League: League fleets in Sarvos, Spiral and Tassato faced Grendel raids and Holberg's fleets suffered from Dho'uala. League priests of Ambition gained liao and Synod votes, and League business upgrades were cheaper during a grand competition.
n.Urizen: Urizen congregations lost votes and liao for a year after the Sulemaine repudiation. Its fleets suffered Grendel raids, and the Icy Maw halved mana output in Redoubt and Morrow.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets once again lost production to the eerie presence of Dho'uala in the Semmerlak.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk fleets could now sail from Caitun to hunt monsters in the Sea of Snow for weltsilver and other rewards.

t.Astolat: Astolat hosted part of the Grand Tour, a series of extraordinary tourneys celebrating Dawn's greatest quest.
t.Bregasland: Magistrates descended in force on Bregasland to investigate its households and root out traitors, disrupting every personal resource there until the Winter Solstice.
t.Casinea: A curse brought bad weather to Casinea and froze still pools into mirrors showing the spectres of those the onlookers had wronged.
t.Feroz: Imperial fleets in Feroz suffered from independent Grendel raids. The Atalaya Harbour discount on fleet upgrades would last only while the Freeborn did not control Feroz.
t.Holberg: Holberg's fleets again lost production to the menace of Dho'uala in the Semmerlak.
t.Madruga: The Atalaya Harbour in Madruga made fleet upgrades cost one less wain of weirwood.
t.Morrow: The Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence ritual halved the output of every mana site in Morrow this season.
t.Redoubt: The Icy Maw Devours the Spark of Essence ritual halved the output of every mana site in Redoubt this season.
t.Sarvos: Imperial fleets in Sarvos suffered from independent Grendel attacks on their ships after the peace treaty ended.
t.Sea of Snow: With Caitun's port expanded, Freeborn, Marcher and Winterfolk fleets could hunt the Sea of Snow's monsters for weltsilver and rarer prizes such as kraken's ink.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm hosted part of the Grand Tour tourneys celebrating the completion of Dawn's greatest quest.
t.Spiral: Imperial fleets in Spiral suffered from independent Grendel attacks on their ships after the peace treaty ended.
t.Tassato: Imperial fleets in Tassato suffered from independent Grendel attacks on their ships after the peace treaty ended.
t.The Semmerlak: The sovereign Dho'uala continued to haunt the Semmerlak with eerie lights and disappearances, raising prices for the Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks and the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater hosted part of the Grand Tour tourneys celebrating the completion of Dawn's greatest quest.

385YE Winter Solstice winds of fortune.d: Alongside the coronation, the winds cover Senate appraisals on the Spider's Dream Tollbridge and new roads, and responses from eternals to plenipotentiary missives. Cold Sun's scions struck sites across the Empire, with mixed results. Other entries cover the Marchers embracing the Mournwold Orcs, the Doctrine of Enlightenment, the shattering of the sword scholars and Urizen rebels in Spiral. Night Below stirs beneath Varushkan mountains, the Deadwood Knight and a horror trouble the Semmerlak, and the Great Library of Hacynian has found a way to end the vallorn. Further items cover rewards for those who broke the vyig, a Grendel-hostile Bay, an auction for Emperor Barabbas's fleet, the Free Folk preparing to join the Empire, trade conditions and the outcomes of the Autumn conjunctions.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Lady Clarice Novarion saw the Doctrine of Enlightenment replace Human Destiny. Residents of Weirwater face the Deadwood Knight, and Dawn is named among those offered the General of Day's boons.
n.Druj: The Druj were driven out of the Barrens by the Golden Sun, and their plan at the Well of Tears was foiled. They still hold the Vate's Shelter in Sarangrave and escaped into Brocéliande from Murderdale.
n.Grendel: Grendel armadas have struck back at the Brass Coast in the Bay of Catazar, targeting and boarding fleets, and their port of Oran remains closed to Imperial ships.
n.Highguard: The Highborn are called to arms against Cold Sun around the Granite Pillar in Bastion. Their priests are helping the Imperial Orcs strengthen their nation, and Highguard is among the nations invited to bid for Barabbas's fleet.
n.Imperial Orcs: Highborn priests identified six ways for the septs of Skarsind to strengthen the young nation. The Halls of Worth were saved from the scions, and several Imperial Orcs are named among the champions who broke the vyig.
n.Jotun: Imperial heroes captured the Blue Eel banner and Mathilda Fisher in Tromsa, recovered a Jotun cache and drove off a Jotun warband. Elsewhere, the Lasambrian Jotun have invaded Kahraman.
n.Navarr: The expanded Great Library of Hacynian has revealed a way to destroy the vallorn. Scions ravaged the trods in Hercynia, and the Great Forest Orcs returned home in the Barrens with the Quiet Step's aid.
n.The Brass Coast: The blight has devoured the Great Grasses of Madruga, and Grendel are raiding Freeborn fleets in the Bay. The Freeborn Assembly is seeking to take the fight back, and the nation is invited to bid for Barabbas's fleet.
n.The League: The League saw the end of the great city contest and consolidated its hold on Spiral despite Urizen rebels. Its businesses promise rewards to the League citizens who helped break the vyig.
n.The Marches: The Marches welcomed the first Marcher Orcs and face bad blood in Bregasland as Mathilda Fisher arrives. The heralds have located the Vorpal Sword of Tom Drake.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule businesswarlocks are among the visitors to Anvil looking for investors.
n.Urizen: The Urizen assembly shattered the sword scholars and the Temple of the Four Winds, while rebel Urizen hold out in Spiral. A Winter curse has settled on Morrow and Redoubt, and Varushkan miners seek Urizen lightstones.
n.Varushka: Night Below has grown more active beneath Volodmartz and Miekarova and has a proposal concerning the Shepherds of Ash. Karov faces the Deadwood Knight, and several Varushkans are listed among the vyig-breakers.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark assembly has an opportunity to act against threats from the dark and cold, and Mathilda Fisher is to be delivered to the Wintermark camp. Wintermark fleets gain a bonus trading with Faraden's port of Caitun.

t.Bastion: Highborn armies defend the Granite Pillar against Cold Sun, and scions claimed the ruins of the White Tower and built a fortification there.
t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel are targeting and boarding fleets in the Bay. The Duke of Arbonne will auction rights to Barabbas's fleet, inviting nations bordering the Bay.
t.Bregasland: Bregasland is divided between supporters and opponents of Mathilda Fisher while magistrates hunt collaborators. Scions also seized the Still Rock in Gravenmarch.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Druj and the lieutenant of Yaw'nagrah escaped into Brocéliande from Murderdale.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the people of Casinea are among those tagged as affected by the winds of magic.
t.Hahnmark: Scions were prevented from slaughtering the Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming at White Owl Fields in Kronemark.
t.Hercynia: Scions ravaged Hercynia's trods, cutting the vallorn there off from the network.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun invasion of Kahraman may explain fewer traders arriving from Faraden.
t.Karov: The Deadwood Knight's challenge to Karov has gone wrong, and scions slaughtered workers in Wieliczka to claim mithril.
t.Karsk: Scions were stopped at Gulgisaz in Nitrost, and the vale of Veresk still stands.
t.Madruga: The blight has consumed the Great Grasses, making the region uninhabitable, and the rains containing it may not continue.
t.Miekarova: The sovereign Night Below lurks beneath Miekarova's mountains, threatening miners who seek better illumination.
t.Morrow: A potent Winter curse lies on Morrow. Scions were stopped from unleashing the Peregro hot springs, and an agent of the Rising Tide returned from Morrow with a proposal for the Basilisk of the Bourse.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos remain angry about Imperial involvement in the failure of their venture there with the Grendel.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold Orcs have begun joining the Marches. Quiet Charlie escaped at Southmoor, and a cordial talk took place with Hap the Soft in Green March.
t.Redoubt: A Winter curse weighs on Redoubt, and scions claimed mithril from the Brilliant Star mines in Tomari, permanently altering them.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The conjunction to capture Sarra Grubfeast here was not taken, and her fate is unknown.
t.Sarangrave: The Vate's Shelter in Nesustak Forest remains held by the Druj ghulai.
t.Sarvos: A debt was balanced peacefully at Bertram's Square in Cigno.
t.Segura: Scions raided the Cerevado Nets in Lucksprings and stole a large amount of ilium.
t.Skarsind: Highborn priests identified opportunities for each of Skarsind's six septs, and scions were prevented from destroying the Halls of Worth.
t.Spiral: Spiral remains split between the League and Urizen rebels, some of whose demands have been met while others are still being negotiated.
t.Temeschwar: The Company of the Torch was brought decisively to justice in Polseg Woods in Vardstein Vale.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens are soaked in blood after the Druj expulsion and the slaughter of several orc factions, and the Well of Tears was warded against the Druj.
t.The Semmerlak: A horror lurks in the Semmerlak, and her servants exact a grim tithe from those crossing the lake.
t.Tromsa: Imperial heroes captured the Blue Eel banner and Mathilda Fisher here, recovered Grimnir's Glass and a Jotun cache, and drove off a Jotun warband.
t.Upwold: Heroes went to deal with the Drakes Dozen at Tom's Dale on the Heath; the outcome is unknown.
t.Volodmartz: Night Below has grown more active beneath Volodmartz's mountains, endangering miners.
t.Weirwater: The Deadwood Knight's challenge to the people of Weirwater has been met, but something seems to have gone wrong.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: At the Broken Holt, scions claimed the ruins of the White Tower and constructed a fortification.
r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: At Harry's Field, scions claimed the Still Rock, disrupting Graven Rock and bringing forth another magical army.
r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: At White Owl Fields, scions were prevented from slaughtering the Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: At Danwyn's Coppice, scions ravaged the trods, cutting Hercynia's vallorn off from the network.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: At the Thicket of Nieshka, scions slaughtered the workers and claimed a large amount of mithril.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: At Gulgisaz, scions were stopped and the vale of Veresk still stands.
r.Morrow/Peregro: At Seneca's Meadow, scions were stopped before they could unleash the destructive power of the Peregro hot springs.
r.Mournwold/Green March: At Golden Hoof Farm, Bloodcrow Knott held a cordial conversation with Hap the Soft.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: At Crowned Trees, Brother Martin Orchard's meeting with Quiet Charlie was disrupted, and Charlie escaped.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: From Magnus' Thicket, scions entered the Brilliant Star, took a large amount of mithril and permanently altered the mines.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: At the Queen's Claim, the attempt to reclaim the Vate's Shelter failed, and it remains with the Druj ghulai.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: At Bertram's Square, the Dramaturgists of the League resolved a debt peacefully.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: On the Path to Cerevado, scions raided the Cerevado Nets and stole a large amount of ilium.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: At Oathwright's Glade, scions were prevented from destroying the Halls of Worth.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: In Polseg Woods, the Company of the Torch was brought decisively to justice.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: At Hugh's Sward, the attempt to slay the Lady of the Dappled Trees failed as the Druj and Yaw'nagrah's lieutenant escaped into Brocéliande.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: At the Grove of Einar, Grimnir's Glass was recovered.
r.Tromsa/Rikskog: At Fniskard Copse, Imperial heroes recovered a Jotun cache.
r.Tromsa/Tromsdalen: At Nordbotn, a Jotun warband was driven off from the palisade, preventing reinforcements reaching Oksenesfestsal.
r.Upwold/The Heath: At Tom's Dale, heroes went to deal with the Drakes Dozen; the outcome is unknown.

385YE Winter Solstice winds of war.d: Peace with the Grendel ended. Sarvos, Redoubt, Necropolis and the City of Masks braced for attack, but the whole Grendel armada fell on Madruga. Siroc was taken, then burned by their Asavean allies, and the territory was lost to the Empire, though not claimed by the orcs. Imperial armies headed for Mareave, four armies pursued separate courses in the Barrens, and the Jotun war in the west continued. Sentinel Gate opportunities included rescuing trapped Dawnish knights-errant in Greenweald, performing the Dance of Navarr and Thorn at the Circle of Rot in Sweetglades, and stopping heralds across several territories. The generals would choose two of three battle opportunities: two in Madruga and one in Mareave.

n.Dawn: The Emerald Dogs, Dawnish knights-errant sent by Earl Phillip Borpusip, were trapped by vallornspawn in Greenweald, and the Knight of the Greenwood, Percival Summerstrong, was charged with their rescue. A further conjunction sought to stop heralds in Astolat.
n.Grendel: Having ended the peace, the Grendel sent their entire armada against Madruga, took Siroc and overran the territory, while Imperial forces prepared to fight them at Coursmouth, Naris, Uccelini and in Mareave.
n.Highguard: The faithful defended the White City in Bastion against Cold Sun's monstrous attackers, and the Necropolis chapters stood ready against the Grendel. The Champion of Loyalty was charged with reclaiming or destroying Oath-heart at Sybella Cross.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: listed with a small force weight available for the coming battles.
n.Jotun: Jotun warriors continued a tense contest of manoeuvre with Imperial soldiers in the west, and conjunctions were offered to stop the Jarl of Greenwall in Skallahn and Jotun forces in Liathaven.
n.Navarr: After Cold Sun damaged Therunin's trods, the stridings found the Circle of Rot regio in Sweetglades. The Spear of the Seven was charged with distracting the vallornspawn so the Archmage of Spring's coven could perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost Madruga as Siroc, the City of Thousand Sails, was taken by the Grendel and burned by their Asavean allies. The Azure Sutannir was charged with rescuing Erdene Bataguin in Kahraman.
n.The League: Sarvos, reinforced by the Ballagruh garrison, and the City of Masks, guarded by the Wolves of War and the Fire of the South, both braced for Grendel retribution that had not come by the Solstice.
n.The Marches: Marcher lands were the focus of a conjunction to stop heralds at Sammy's Paling in Upwold, and Marcher armies held particular strategic advantages when fighting in their home territories.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov was named as responsible for rescuing captives on the Siroc Plains in Madruga.
n.Urizen: Sentinels from Cargo joined the citadels and spires of Redoubt in watching for Grendel ships near the new port at Elos. The Elosian Architect was charged with defeating the Grendel at the Elosian Grove.
n.Varushka: Varushka was named among the lands suffering the destruction wrought by the scions of Cold Sun, and the Senator for Miekarova was charged with returning villagers to their barrow in Perumaki.
n.Wintermark: Cold Sun's assault reached Hahnmark, and conjunctions were offered to stop heralds in Kronemark and Kallavesa Marsh, while Winterfolk armies continued to fight the Jotun with honour.

t.Astolat: A conjunction was offered to stop the heralds at the Coppice of Roses in Groveyard, under the Knight-protector of Autumn.
t.Bastion: The faithful of the Empire protected the White City from Cold Sun's monstrous attackers, and a conjunction sought to reclaim or destroy Oath-heart at Tamar's Stand.
t.Bay of Catazar: After the peace collapsed, Imperial sentinels across the Bay watched the sea for the Grendel, whose mastery of the waters the new port at Elos could threaten. Orc pirates attacked merchant vessels before the armada struck Madruga.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: noted as a place where the Strong Reeds held a strategic advantage until they left the territory.
t.Brocéliande: The Emerald Dogs knights-errant were cut off by vallornspawn in Greenweald, and a rescue was to be mounted through the Sentinel Gate.
t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark was among the lands assailed by the scions of Cold Sun, and a conjunction was offered to stop the heralds at Dun's Hurst.
t.Kahraman: A conjunction was offered on the Path of Idina in Gambit to rescue Erdene Bataguin, under the Azure Sutannir.
t.Kallavesa: A conjunction was offered to stop the heralds on the Road to Masi, under the Woundbinder of the Mark.
t.Liathaven: A conjunction was offered to stop the Jotun at the Bawn of Daffyd, under the Imperial Advisor for the Feni.
t.Madruga: The entire Grendel armada assailed Madruga, took Siroc, which their Asavean allies then burned, and looted the territory, leaving it lost to the Empire but unclaimed by the orcs. Battle opportunities targeted the Lyceum and the Shining Pillar.
t.Mareave: Imperial armies marched down the Apulian Way into the Broken Shore, and a battle opportunity was offered to influence Mareave's complex politics.
t.Miaren: A conjunction was offered to stop the heralds at the Golden Meadow, under the Spear of the Seven.
t.Miekarova: A conjunction was offered to return villagers to their barrow at Wilkza in Perumaki, under the territory's senator.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory where Imperial armies may billet and Marcher armies hold an advantage.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: noted for the defensive advantage Highborn and Urizen armies hold there against attacks from Zenith.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: listed as a territory where Marcher armies hold an advantage when fighting.
t.Necropolis: Reumah's Rest and the chapters at Crown's Quay stood vigilant against Grendel attack, and a conjunction was offered to defeat the Grendel at Hedra's Meadow in Coursmouth.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: noted as a place where Varushkan armies may call on the hospitality of the boyars.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: appears only in the title of the Ambassador to Otkodov, named as responsible for a rescue in Madruga.
t.Redoubt: Sentinels from Cargo came to Naris to join Redoubt's citadels in watching for the Grendel near Elos, and a conjunction was offered to defeat the Grendel at the Elosian Grove.
t.Sarvos: Expecting Grendel retribution, the City of Nets was reinforced by the Ballagruh garrison, though no attack had come by the Solstice. A conjunction was offered to defeat the Grendel on the Isle of Quiet.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Emerald Dogs set out into the forests south of Semmerholm.
t.Skallahn: A conjunction was offered at Hralfstor's Orchard in Iron Stand to stop the Jarl of Greenwall.
t.Spiral: The Ballagruh garrison marched beneath the shadow lying over Spiral to reinforce Sarvos, troubled by dark dreams.
t.The Barrens: Four Imperial armies operated in the Barrens, each pursuing its own course and profoundly affecting the people they passed.
t.Therunin: After Cold Sun damaged its trods, a Spring regio at the Circle of Rot offered a chance to perform the Dance of Navarr and Thorn, if heroes could distract the vallornspawn massed there.
t.Upwold: A conjunction was offered to stop the heralds at Sammy's Paling on the Heath. Imperial armies may also billet in the territory.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: noted for the advantage Highborn and Urizen armies hold when attacking into it from Morrow.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: The Champion of Loyalty was charged with reclaiming or destroying Oath-heart at Tamar's Stand.
r.Brocéliande/Greenweald: Surviving Emerald Dogs knights-errant were trapped by vallornspawn here, and the Knight of the Greenwood was to lead a rescue to Crangton Copse.
r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: The Caretaker of New Dunhall was charged with stopping the heralds at Dun's Hurst.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: A conjunction to the Path of Idina sought to rescue Erdene Bataguin.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: A conjunction to the Road to Masi sought to stop the heralds.
r.Liathaven/Liaven's Glen: A conjunction to the Bawn of Daffyd sought to stop the Jotun.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: The Hakima of Salt and Sand was charged with reclaiming an heirloom at Ezmara's Thicket.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: The Spear of the Seven was charged with stopping the heralds at the Golden Meadow.
r.Miekarova/Perumaki: A largely non-combat conjunction to Wilkza sought to return villagers to their barrow.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: The Champion of Courage was charged with defeating the Grendel at Hedra's Meadow.
r.Necropolis/Hedrossan: Mentioned in passing: not named directly. The page describes Necropolis as a whole standing vigilant against the Grendel.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Sentinels from Cargo gathered at Naris to watch for Grendel ships, and the Elosian Architect was charged with defeating the Grendel at the Elosian Grove.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: The Custodian of Glass Point Cove was charged with defeating the Grendel on the Isle of Quiet.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Mentioned in passing: appears only in the title of the Jarl of Greenwall, whom Imperial heroes were asked to stop in Iron Stand.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: The Imperial Seer was charged with stopping the Jarl of Greenwall at Hralfstor's Orchard.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the thing that squats in Screed fed the fears and dark dreams of the Ballagruh garrison.
r.Therunin/Sweetglades: Vallornspawn massed around the Circle of Rot, where heroes were to distract them while a coven performed the Dance of Navarr and Thorn.
r.Upwold/The Heath: The Custodian of Sutton Stone Quarries was charged with stopping the heralds at Sammy's Paling.

A Crown in Winter.d: Raised on a pumpkin farm in Srodkoja, Vesna joined the Wardens of the Grateful Hearth and served two terms as senator for Ossium, extending the Iron Roads. She faced inquisition over the Winter 383YE treaty with the Thule, without further resolution. No veto was sought in time, so the Constitutional Court confirmed she would take the Throne at the first Senate session, first ratifying her own election. Planned celebrations included a timed tour of the nations, national presentations, a dedication to Prosperity by Ophelia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato, and a crowning by Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost. The Commonwealth, Faraden, Axos, Otkodov and Sarcophan said they would send representatives with gifts.

n.Dawn: The Empress's tour would reach the Dawnish at 14:50, and Dawn would make the second formal presentation at the coronation ceremony.
n.Highguard: Highguard would be the second nation visited on the tour, at 13:40, and would give the third presentation to the new Throne.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs would welcome the Empress at 14:20 and present fourth. Emperor Ahraz's coronation during the Orc Rebellion was recalled as a precedent for celebrating even in wartime.
n.Navarr: The Navarr would welcome the Empress at 14:30 and give the seventh formal presentation.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast would be the final stop on the tour, at 15:00, and would open the national presentations at the ceremony.
n.The League: The League would welcome the Empress at 14:10 and present fifth, and Ophelia Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato of the League would perform the coronation's dedication to Prosperity.
n.The Marches: The Marches would receive the Empress at 14:00 and give the sixth presentation at the ceremony.
n.Thule: Vesna's part in the Winter 383YE treaty with the Thule led to her being called before an inquisition, and Thule-held Otkodov planned to send a representative to acknowledge her accession.
n.Urizen: Urizen would be the third nation on the tour, at 13:50, and would give the eighth presentation.
n.Varushka: A Varushkan from Srodkoja and former senator for Ossium became Empress-elect, crowned by Belakov Zakharovich Prochnost with an anthem by Kalina Jadwigowna Piosnkowa Prochnost. Her tour would begin in Varushka at 13:30, and Varushka would give the ninth presentation.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark would welcome the Empress at 14:40 and give the final national presentation at the ceremony.

t.Miekarova: The new Empress-elect was raised in Miekarova, on a pumpkin farm in the woods of its region of Srodkoja.
t.Otkodov: The government of Otkodov, then held by the Thule, said it would send a representative to Anvil to acknowledge the new Empress.

r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: Srodkoja was Vesna's home: the youngest of seven children, she grew up on a pumpkin farm in its woods before joining the Wardens of the Grateful Hearth.

A Sparrow in Spring.d: The Senate could name one person, by a single motion, to organise celebrations with Imperial funds, Synod Virtue fund money and private donations. Grand celebrations cost 80 thrones, breath-taking ones 250 and wondrous ones 500. The scale set the benefit, while the Throne's short celebratory message set its nature, as when Empress Lisabetta's 500-throne festivities and her plea to stem the tide of Imperial blood let every army launch a steady conquest. Empress Vesna also had to ratify her own election and the creation of the Citizen's Voice. She could appoint the Captain of the Throne Guard and the Queen's Rose, and had to decide whether to seek the vacant title of Monarch of Dawn.

n.Dawn: Dawnish weavers were booked up with orders for fine garments, the new Empress could appoint the long-vacant Queen's Rose, and she had to decide whether to claim the vacant title of Monarch of Dawn. Any such claim would rely wholly on Dawnish nobles fighting for her in the tourney.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League's cities were recalled as transformed into wonderlands during Empress Lisabetta's coronation celebrations.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: breath-taking celebrations would include magical lights imported from Urizen, and past festivities had linked its spires with bridges of magical glass.
n.Varushka: The new Empress was a Varushkan, and wealthy Varushkans were determined that her celebrations would be as magnificent as those of the Merchant Prince of Holberg. The page noted the recent closeness between Varushka and Dawn, whose armies fought side by side to conquer Ossium.

t.Bay of Catazar: Merchants on the Bay of Catazar had begun importing consignments of wine, beer, brandy and mead in anticipation of the festivities.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Varushkans hoped to match the Prosperity shown for Empress Lisabetta, the Merchant Prince of Holberg.
t.Ossium: Excitement ran highest in Ossium, where every town and vale was preparing to celebrate the new Empress. The territory had been conquered by Varushkan and Dawnish armies fighting side by side.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: donations after Emperor James's coronation went much of the way towards repairing the Tower of the Dawn in the Barrens.

A beacon of smoke.d: Treachery from within Siroc and Naguerro battle-magic brought down the Salt Guard's chains and twin keeps, despite Autumn enchantments, a Freeborn warband and the Commonwealth Embassy garrison. The Grendel looted Siroc, then the Asaveans burned it and murdered captured priests. Friends of the Prince of a Thousand Foes led many people, including the Kindled Flame's orphans, to safety. Quzar, the Parador of Salt and Sand, Atalaya, Midport and the Shining Pillar fell, and the Lyceum came under siege. Madruga lost its Senator and several titles lost their ministries. Solstice opportunities were offered to raise the Lyceum's wards, save the Shining Pillar and counter Grendel raids elsewhere.

n.Grendel: Their armada of four navies and several armies, including the Iron Gulls, Black Eels, Bone Nautilus and Governor Rahab's troops, took Siroc Plains, Lightsea and Free Landing, looting the Sapphire and besieging the Lyceum. Their captains also launched probing raids across the Bay.
n.Highguard: Grendel Sky Mage Ranald, who escaped the purge of an espionage ring in Necropolis, was moving through Coursmouth to uncover a secret guarded by the chapter of Ethan's Respite. The Champion of Courage, Thomir, Son of Astion, was charged with stopping him.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost Siroc, Lightsea and Free Landing, along with the Shining Pillar, the Freeborn Flame Marina and several ministries, and Madruga's Senate seat. Short of the prosperous coastal regions, their armies would begin to decline after the Winter Solstice.
n.The League: The Salt Guard, designed by Menno van Ritsjhof, was destroyed. Grendel raiders under Quartermaster Ewan threatened Glass Point Cove in Sarvos, and the Sarvos Shipwrights Syndicate offered fleet deeds in return for salvaging defeated Grendel ships.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Marches are not named on the page. The nearest related matter is the destruction of the Commonwealth Embassy in Siroc and the Ambassador to the Commonwealth losing their ministry.
n.Urizen: Maistir Dorcas landed in Naris to threaten the Great Harbour of Elos, and the Elosian Architect, Talia Seaboar, was offered the fleet deed to The Impulse for stopping them. A recovered Final Dance of the Immobile could also be added to Urizen lore.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the iron chains and nets that guarded Siroc's harbour had been imported centuries ago from the forges of Wintermark.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel armada and Asavean warships swept across the Bay to strike Madruga, and individual Grendel captains raided targets around its shores. With the Shining Pillar dark, the Bay lost its familiar beacon.
t.Feroz: Governor Rahab's honour guard sailed from Grendel-held Feroz to join the assault and looted the Glass Parador. The earlier loss of Feroz helped leave the Brass Coast unable to supply its armies.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: Hahnmark is not named; Wintermark appears only as the source of Siroc's old harbour chains.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Iñez i Azul-Mar i Erigo of Kahraman, captain of the Bloodgold Jackals, is listed in the Freeborn force table.
t.Madruga: Siroc was razed and left in ruins, and the Grendel took three of the territory's six regions. Madruga became contested and lost its Senator, though the Lyceum's wards and the Shining Pillar might yet be saved.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is not named anywhere on the page.
t.Necropolis: With its defenders watching the coast, Sky Mage Ranald's reduced company was heading for Ada's Plain and the Courspan Bridge. The Champion of Courage was asked to intercept them.
t.Redoubt: Grendel under Maistir Dorcas, accompanied by heralds of the Mother of Wrecks, were marching on the shipyards and warehouses of Elos.
t.Sarvos: Grendel raiders threatened Glass Point Cove and its mithril netting. The Sarvos Shipwrights Syndicate agreed to salvage captured Grendel ships in return for granting fleet deeds.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: refugees from Siroc, including the orphans of the Parador of the Kindled Flame, fled west across the Scorrero toward Segura.

r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: Mentioned in passing: it is listed as one of the prosperous coastal regions, two of which the Freeborn would need to regain to supply their armies again.
r.Feroz/Fontargenta: Mentioned in passing: it is listed as one of the prosperous coastal regions whose recovery would help restore Freeborn army supply.
r.Feroz/Oranseri: Mentioned in passing: it is listed as one of the prosperous coastal regions whose recovery would help restore Freeborn army supply.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: It remained in Freeborn hands, as the Salt Guard's resistance slowed the armada too much to attack it. Holding Calvos is essential to the Brass Coast's hopes of resupplying its armies.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: The Grendel seized Atalaya, Midport and the Shining Pillar, whose beacon went out, and besieged the Lyceum. Battles were offered to raise the Lyceum's wards, rescue the Beacon's Watch and stop an Asavean sacrifice.
r.Madruga/Lightsea: Grendel forces overran Lightsea, taking Quzar and looting the Parador of Salt and Sand. Sand Mage Nechtan waited at Ezmara's Thicket to escape with a stolen hakima heirloom.
r.Madruga/Torres: Mentioned in passing: Torres is noted as one of only two Madrugan regions still under Freeborn control.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Sky Mage Ranald's company was moving through Coursmouth towards Ada's Plain, with the Sentinel Gate opening to Hedra's Meadow.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Maistir Dorcas landed on the Naris coast and left a guard at the ships while hurrying toward Elos. The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Elosian Grove.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Quartermaster Ewan landed on a wooded Uccelini island with servants of the Salt-born Devourer, sending a vanguard ahead to Glass Point Cove. The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Isle of Quiet.

A thousand years of longing.d: With contributions from the League, Highborn pilgrims, the Department of Historical Research, the eternal Phaleron, papers seized from the Heirs of Terunael and Thule scholars from Otkodov, the library confirmed and extended Siân Eternal's work. It traced the vallorn to Terunael rituals meant to channel Spring magic into their armies. Scholars set out three futures: centuries more trod-walking, the Heirs' spreading of the vallorn, or connecting the last unlinked hearts, Béantal Dol in Sarangrave and Cavan in Visokuma, to provoke a final war that the Empire might win but could not easily halt. Opportunities included spying on Béantal Dol, approaching eternals and Assembly statements. Spymaster Bernard Dugdale funded the Sarangrave expedition.

n.Druj: The Druj are thought to have studied and contained the vallorn of Béantal Dol, possibly from the Palace of the Sleepers, and may be researching magic to rouse it, so liberating Sarangrave from them is seen as the likely first step towards the final trod.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: in the opening story a Navarr scholar expects the Senate to say the time is not right until the Druj and the Grendel have been dealt with.
n.Highguard: Highborn pilgrims supplied books and priceless journals dating back to landfall, their grey pilgrims are credited with speeding the weakening of the vallorn, and the Highborn Assembly is one of two assemblies whose mandates on the findings other nations' priests could answer.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named, though Liathaven, which they hold, is noted as having one remaining vallorn region and disrupted trods.
n.Navarr: The Navarr now hold everything there is to know about the vallorn and face an existential choice: keep walking the trods for centuries or complete the network and fight the final battle that Navarr and Thorn foresaw, which would also end their trapped ancestors' lives.
n.Thule: Otkodov's orc warlocks and their Dragons shared ancient records and are enthusiastically in favour of completing the trod network, promising to deal with Sküld's vallorn themselves, apparently hoping to restore Sküld and reach the treasures of Emrys.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the Terunael used ilium taken from the Urizen to power their rituals, and a scattering of Urizen arcane scholars agreed that a roused vallorn would take years to subside.

t.Brocéliande: Brocéliande remains the gravest threat with five vallorn regions, an ancient vallorn whose heart holds Navarr and Thorn, and papers from the Heirs of Terunael stronghold there shaped the library's findings; Wither the Seed's restraint would fail once its curse ends or the vallorn is roused.
t.Hercynia: Home of the Great Library, whose work went on undeterred by the threat of Cold Sun, Hercynia has one vallorn region left; its recently disrupted trods let the vallorn recover, and its heart is thought likely the next to become vulnerable in perhaps fifty years.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven has one vallorn region left, but its disrupted trods let the vallorn recover quickly, its reclamation was projected at a century beyond Hercynia, and it would return to full force once Wither the Seed runs its course.
t.Miaren: Miaren holds the only vallorn heart ever destroyed, and its records show the vallorn lashing out when exposed and decades of clearing afterwards, which is why it is so lightly forested.
t.Otkodov: A contingent of orc warlocks from Otkodov joined the Great Library's faculty, bringing Thule scrolls never seen by human eyes and warning that a fully roused vallorn could not quickly be stopped.
t.Sarangrave: Sarangrave contains Béantal Dol, one of only two unconnected vallorn hearts, so its liberation is likely needed for the final trod; Imperial Spymaster Bernard Dugdale backed the spy network there to scout the vallorn heart.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin is listed as still holding two vallorn regions, among the smaller vallorn that would fight savagely if roused.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Mentioned in passing: Dark Ranging is cited, alongside West Ranging, as becoming vulnerable within the same decade thanks to the trods' wider reach and more travellers.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: The vallorn of Terunael, the first and most potent, is where Navarr and Thorn led their final expedition and where they seem to remain alive at the heart, keeping the vallorn from healing so the trods can bleed it.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: The fight to clear the vallorn from West Ranging is cited as showing how a weakened vallorn rises in frenzy yet can then be defeated.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Site of the Terunael city of Emrys, Sküld's vallorn is constrained and weakened under Thule Winter magic; the Thule offer to destroy it themselves if it is roused, which would let them restore the region's fertility and perhaps reach Emrys.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: The Dance of Navarr and Thorn would have to be cast in Bendol to link Béantal Dol to the trods, and the Spymaster's 6 wains of weirwood funded a season's outpost there to scout the vallorn heart, leading to the Into Béantal Dol report.

Against the Jotun.d: After capturing Mathilda Fisher, the Empire retreated into Sermersuaq, and Yrsa Jansdóttir's forces retook Tromsa. The Bloodcloaks, Green Shield, Red Wind Corsairs, Summer Storm and Tusks, with over sixty captains, attacked the Iron Stand but met four southern Jotun armies. After a pre-battle toast with Bjorgthorn Hammerhand, three days of fighting left a stalemate. The Empire is a quarter of the way to taking the Iron Stand, and honourable Wintermark fighting reduced its casualties by a tenth. Summer Storm orcs heard a new ancestral voice in their fighting pits. In Kahraman, Lasambrian raids halted road restoration, delayed the Red Depths and left Gambit three-fifths conquered. Three Sentinel Gate opportunities were also announced.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Mouse of Dawn, Sebastián Fawnwood and Urien Novarion are listed among the captains who fought in Skallahn.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm fought in the Iron Stand, and many Skarsind captains joined the campaign. Sunstorm orcs who tested themselves in the army's fighting pits heard an unnamed ancestral voice urging them to fierce loyalty to family and vengeance on traitors.
n.Jotun: Under Yrsa Jansdóttir, the Jotun reclaimed Tromsa. Four southern armies with local fyrds held the Iron Stand to a stalemate, and the Lasambrian Jotun raided Kahraman and pressed towards the conquest of Gambit.
n.The Brass Coast: The Red Wind Corsairs fought with notable restraint in Skallahn, helping to bury an old Winterfolk slur against the Freeborn. Meanwhile, Kahraman suffered a fresh Lasambrian invasion that halted its great Senate projects.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Viktor von Temeschwar is listed among the captains, and an unnamed League general is quoted on contingency planning.
n.The Marches: Marcher armies led the vanguard in Tromsa, and the Tusks fought in the Iron Stand. The Imperial Advisor for the Feni was offered a chance to atone for the Alderly killings by saving a Feni enclave in Liathaven.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Aulus Warcaster of Zenith is listed among the captains and named by the Bloodcloaks' general.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Maria Alexandrovna Kabanova of Ossium is listed among the captains fighting in Skallahn.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield fought with honour in the Iron Stand, earning Jotun respect and mutual quarter that cut Wintermark casualties by a tenth. The Imperial Seer was asked to lead a strike on Jarl Ebbe.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Mouse of Dawn, a captain from Astolat, fought in the Skallahn campaign.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Marcher captains from Bregasland are listed among those in Skallahn, and scions of Cold Sun are said to have been seen there.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: many Hahnmark captains are listed, including Lofyn Blood-cloak and the warriors of Dunhearth Hall.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: Hordalant is not named in the page and is linked only through the wider Jotun campaign.
t.Kahraman: The Lasambrians invaded again, seizing about ten wains of white granite and halting road restoration. Work on the Red Depths is delayed until the Spring Equinox, and a Sentinel Gate opportunity was announced to rescue a captured Faraden architect.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: several Kallavesa captains are listed among those fighting in Skallahn.
t.Liathaven: A warband under Urse Longarm is moving to breach the wards of a hidden Feni enclave in Liathaven. The Imperial Advisor for the Feni was charged with stopping them via the Sentinel Gate.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold captains are listed among those in Skallahn, and heralds of the Mother of Wrecks are recalled as having appeared there.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: Mournwold captains are listed, the dour Mournish are quoted, and Halka was sighted in Freemoor.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Maria Alexandrovna Kabanova of Ossium is listed among the captains.
t.Reinos: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun warband holding Erdene Bataguin is heading back towards the border with Reinos.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: those fighting alongside the Burning Falcon in Segura are referenced for comparison.
t.Sermersuaq: The Imperial armies retreated from Tromsa into Sermersuaq and rested briefly before invading Skallahn. Several Sermersuaq captains, including Iron Osric, joined the campaign.
t.Skallahn: The Imperial invasion of the Iron Stand met four southern Jotun armies and stalled below Oversgaard after three days of heavy fighting. The Empire is a quarter of the way to taking the region, and Jarl Ebbe is calling up a fyrd.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: numerous Skarsind captains are listed, and the page muses on a possible new understanding between Jotun and Skarsind.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Viktor von Temeschwar is listed among the captains.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: Sebastián Fawnwood of the Barrens is listed among the captains.
t.Tromsa: The Empire defeated Igya Olgafsdottir's warriors and took Mathilda Fisher before withdrawing. The Jotun then swiftly reconquered every region the Empire had taken.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold captains of the Hartell Household are listed among those in Skallahn.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Urien Novarion of Weirwater is listed among the captains.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Aulus Warcaster, called the Dragon of Zenith, is listed among the captains.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: Lasambrian soldiers reached the region and paid respects at the Fort Braydon burial mound. A Jotun warband also seized a Bataguin caravan there and took Erdene Bataguin as a thrall.
r.Kahraman/Gambit: The Lasambrians camped in Gambit, taking villages and estates, and are over three-fifths of the way to conquering it. The Sentinel Gate is to open at the Path of Idina.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Lasambrian warbands were sent east to harry the people of the Jade Range.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: A magical citadel was raised in the mountains above Serra Briante, helping to deter the Lasambrians.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: A magical citadel garrisoned by lion-headed ogres stood above Serra Damata and turned back probing Lasambrian scouts.
r.Liathaven/Liath's Heart: Mentioned in passing: the region is not named; the threatened Feni enclave is described only as lying in the depths of Liathaven.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: the earlier killings of the Feni of Alderly are what the Marchers are invited to atone for.
r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Mentioned in passing: Halka, a herald of the Ancient One, was first spotted near the Old Pig in Freemoor.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: The Imperial armies camped briefly at Olgafsdottirshal in Tanikipari, waiting for the Red Wind Corsairs before crossing into Skallahn.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Seer is named as responsible for stopping 'the Jarl of Greenwall', though the opportunity concerns Jarl Ebbe of the Iron Stand.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Three days of fighting below Oversgaard and the fallen Iron Banner ended in stalemate, leaving the Empire a quarter of the way to taking the region. Jarl Ebbe is calling up its fyrd.
r.Skallahn/Ulfrsmoor: The Imperial plan to besiege Ulfrsborg was blocked by the Southern Bear and the Iron Host, with skirmishes fought across eastern Ulfrsmoor.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: The Imperial armies withdrew through the forested borders of the Icewood into Sermersuaq.
r.Tromsa/Majastind: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun response may have been driven by fear that the Empire would despoil Mount Majastind and the graves of the ancestors.
r.Tromsa/Rikskog: An immense Jotun force under Yrsa Jansdóttir entered Rikskog from the south to catch the invaders, arriving too late.

All my magic friends.d: A Winter curse over Casinea made still water freeze and show viewers the spectres of those they had wronged. Highguard's inquisition routed followers of the Whisper Gallery, though three cultists escaped. The Alders-Baart family were struck by sickness. The dead village of Wilkza rose to celebrate Vesna's coronation. Day boggarts plagued Casinean archivists. Odd portents followed Madruga's tragedies. The Lictors praised Ashborn Trosk and promised contracts for the Autumn Hammers. Arhallogen sought a Navarr fane, and the Azoth demanded profound change of the Navarr. Sanvar Isk denied slaving. Kaela challenged Orc and Wintermark banners. Challenge the Iron Duke became uncastable. Tharim offered his knights to the new Throne.

n.Dawn: Scringol the Hunter, a herald of Jaheris, sought representatives of House de Gauvain and Thanàte Sangwine in the Dawnish camp, and Barien's heralds asked for Aldwyn Wyldrose of Dawn and held a challenge scroll for Rillian de Gauvain.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel and their Asavean allies are named as the cause of the brutality visited on Siroc, and their conquest of Feroz as one of Madruga's woes.
n.Highguard: The Highborn endured the Casinea curse and a plague of Day boggarts, while their inquisition exposed dozens of Whisper Gallery dealers and arrested two covens, with three cultists' details passed to Brother Aemon.
n.Imperial Orcs: Heralds of the Lictors praised Ashborn Trosk and planned to offer contracts granting qualities to the new Autumn Hammers at the Spring Equinox, and Kaela challenged Orc banner-bearers to bind their banners for a year.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun Lasambrians are listed among the troubles afflicting Madruga.
n.Navarr: Arhallogen sought a fane creating a Huntsmaster of the Spider King for a Navarr vate, the Wolf Spider brought a hunting challenge for the thorns, and the Azoth said it could transform the Singing Stone only if the nation fundamentally changed.
n.The Brass Coast: In the wake of Siroc's fall, the Three Sisters constellation shone unnaturally bright to the Freeborn, even at Anvil, while the personae of Death and Fortune wandered Madruga laying curses on those who lingered near them.
n.The League: Sanvar Isk, operator of the Loom of Spells in Tassato, sought out League bishops to quash rumours that he used slave labour before auctioning access to the Loom again.
n.Varushka: The dead villagers of Wilkza rose to celebrate Vesna Borkovna Prochnost's coronation and local boyars asked Varushkans to see them back to their barrow, while a herald of Tharim brought an offer of his knights to the new Throne.
n.Wintermark: Kaela's grim legion came to the Tree of Names to bind Wintermark banners to a year-long challenge, and Barien's heralds summoned Ishka and Jaska about their challenges.

t.Brocéliande: Arhallogen preferred his proposed fane to be built in Brocéliande, the Singing Stone the Azoth offered to transform came from there, and one suggested change for the Navarr was abandoning settlements in its vallorn.
t.Casinea: A Winter curse froze Casinea's still waters into mirrors showing the spectres of those the viewer had wronged, and a swarm of Day boggarts harried its archivists and filled its newspapers with rambling articles.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the conquest of Feroz is listed among the troubles the Three Sisters portent was first thought to reflect.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia is named as one of the more civilised places the Navarr might settle if they abandoned the vallorn.
t.Kahraman: After Siroc's fall, the unnaturally bright Three Sisters constellation was also observed over Kahraman.
t.Liathaven: The Azoth suggested the Navarr could fully abandon Liathaven and formally renounce their claim to it as one way to bring about the change it required.
t.Madruga: Scarred by blight and the burning of Siroc, Madruga saw the Three Sisters shine ever brighter and the personae of Death and Fortune roam the land, cursing those who spent long with them.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as one of the more civilised places the Navarr might settle if they abandoned the vallorn.
t.Miekarova: The long-dead village of Wilkza rose from its barrow to celebrate the new Throne, and the Sentinel Gate opened so Varushkans could attend and see the dead returned to rest.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Tharim's black-clad knights are said to be resting in Sarvos.
t.Segura: After Siroc's fall, the unnaturally bright Three Sisters constellation was also observed over Segura.
t.Skarsind: Heralds of the Lictors visited Skarsind to observe the mustering of the Autumn Hammers and were pleased by what they saw, and Janon's heralds sought out the Skarsind College of Pitfighting.
t.Tassato: Broadsheets around the Loom of Spells regio in Tassato insisting Sanvar Isk was not a slaver instead set the salons and taverns gossiping about abductions.
t.Therunin: Therunin was offered as the acceptable alternative site for Arhallogen's fane, and was also named as a civilised place the Navarr might settle if they left the vallorn.

r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Brianna Black Blood identified a suitable regio in Elerael for Arhallogen's proposed fane, the Centipede General's preferred site.
r.Madruga/Torres: The last eyewitness reports placed the wandering personae of Death and Fortune in Torres.
r.Miekarova/Perumaki: The dead village of Wilkza in Perumaki rose to offer twisted hospitality in celebration of the coronation, shrouded in plaguewulf miasma.
r.Therunin/Eastring: A suitable regio in Eastring was identified as the alternative site for Arhallogen's proposed fane.

All those moments.d: The Great Forest Orcs returned to the Heart of Peytaht and sheltered about a hundred survivors from Hope's Rest, but they now feel betrayed and their trust in the Navarr is fraying. The Karass, newly recognised as foreigners, settled old scores and now eye the Rahvin. The Rahvin, sustained by Imperial Orc supplies, expect destruction and secretly seek weapons through the Imperial Orcs. Black Wind prisoners revealed that their army of over four thousand under Alakath the Torn is marching to the Barrens under duress. Many Dawnish welcomed these events. In Sanath, Imperial curses weakened the Druj, who used the Vendarri's fate to rally their subjects. The clash between Synod and Military Council undermined faith in both.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish occupants of the Barrens were broadly pleased by the destruction of the Montanians and the Black Wind, and Dawnish settlement of Hope's Rest could bring chances to develop the area if the Dawnish Assembly encourages it.
n.Druj: Driven from the Barrens and battered by curses in Sanath, the Druj grew fearful but turned the Vendarri's fate into propaganda to recruit warriors, and they were deeply shaken to see the Empire adopt their own ruthless methods.
n.Grendel: The Druj pinned their hopes on the Grendel's war against the Empire, trusting that it would draw Imperial armies away and let them survive and later retake their lost lands.
n.Imperial Orcs: Their Assembly's gift of 75 thrones of supplies kept the Rahvin alive through winter and won their appreciation, and a secret Rahvin delegation is coming to Anvil to seek weapons from them, although arming declared barbarians would risk a charge of treason.
