n.Navarr: The Great Forest Orcs, their closest orc allies, felt betrayed and confronted the Navarr who had accompanied them; it falls to the Navarr to rebuild that trust or watch the orcs leave Therunin and abandon trade in weirwood.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Orcs were named in the Wintermark Assembly's statement as an example of non-Imperial peoples the Empire has long accepted.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan armies were at the heart of the bloodshed: the Northern Eagle slaughtered the Montanians and the Iron Helms executed the Black Wind's leaders, frightening the sept into compliance, which many Dawnish praised and which rattled the Druj.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark Assembly's statement urging the Empire to accept the Barrens peoples rather than put them to the sword was the only one of the Synod's statements of caution to pass with a greater majority, and it was overshadowed by the Military Council's actions.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Valiant Pegasus withdrew from the Salt Flats to Astolat while Imperial magicians cursed Sanath.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs were recalled as having fought alongside the Navarr against the vallorn in Brocéliande.
t.Hercynia: Great Forest Orcs who were encouraged to settle in Hercynia now find their new steadings, and their Navarr friends, in the firing line if relations with the Empire collapse.
t.Miaren: Great Forest Orcs who were encouraged to settle in Miaren now find their new steadings, and their Navarr friends, in the firing line if relations with the Empire collapse.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Mournwold Orcs were cited in a Synod statement as a non-Imperial people the Empire had treated well.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish commentators pointed to Ossium as an earlier victory of the Dawn–Varushka alliance, and the Druj mourned it as ancestral land they had lost.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Imperial curses ravaged Sanath's settlements and herb fields, and the Druj gathered a major force there and spread tales of the Vendarri to recruit, making local orcs increasingly unwilling to speak with Imperials.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens was soaked in blood as the Montanians, the Black Wind leadership and the Vendarri were destroyed, while the Great Forest Orcs returned home and the Black Wind army marched back under Imperial threat.
t.Therunin: Great Forest Orcs in Therunin had begun to discuss asking to stay among the Navarr, but those talks faltered and they may leave unless the Navarr restore their trust.

r.Ossium/Bittershore: The page places the Rahvin, still occupying the mithril mine on Bittershore, gathering mithril to arm themselves for a fight they expect to lose.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens: Mentioned in passing: after the Summer Solstice the Valiant Pegasus had fought to secure a foothold in the Sydathian Fens.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Rahvin in Bitter Strand received the Imperial Orcs' food and supplies, which ensured they would survive the winter.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Great Forest Orcs reclaimed the Heart of Peytaht and its weirwood grove, sheltered survivors from Hope's Rest, and their elders weighed using the weirwood to fortify against the Dawnish.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: About a hundred survivors of the attack on Hope's Rest fled to the Heart of Peytaht, and the area offers development opportunities if the Dawnish Assembly encourages settlement there.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The Dawnish occupants of Murderdale were broadly pleased by the destruction of the Montanians and the Black Wind.

Begins where it ends.d: Cathan Canae sent a castellan to parley, offering one of three generals a boon for the conquests of Ossium, Sermersuaq and Zenith, and a beacon boon to Wintermark warriors. Zakalwe declined but backed his Polemarch in Skallahn. Ephisis proposed a mutual ban on looting Grendel property in exchange for Grendel restraint, and offered Ogila's Tower in Kalpaheim. Surut agreed to parley but refused to abandon the Druj. Sadogua, furious that Varushkans took the Whistling Strand from his realm, suspended all aid and named three possible reparations. The Azoth offered boons against Cold Sun in exchange for amity. Irra Harah would discuss only the Barrens, barring titled Imperials and Varushkans.

n.Dawn: Cathan Canae's herald recalled her warriors fighting Oblivion in Dawn, while Irra Harah's parley will focus solely on what Dawn's forces did in the Barrens.
n.Druj: Surut refused the Winter Archmage's request to withdraw his aid from the Druj, saying their desperation pleases him and he will feast on their fall if they are destroyed.
n.Grendel: Ephisis offered to persuade the Grendel to stop looting and destroying Imperial wealth if the Senate outlawed robbing or destroying Grendel property, while Surut and Cathan Canae both declined to involve themselves against the Grendel.
n.Jotun: Zakalwe's Polemarch marches with the Bloodcloaks against the Jotun in Skallahn, and Zakalwe hopes his herald can discuss the war against the Jotun with the Imperial Seer.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's herald noted that the Spears of the Pines conquered their homeland in the Barrens with Navarr aid.
n.The Brass Coast: Irra Harah was helping the Freeborn at Madruga, and Surut spoke of the inferno of bitterness the Broken Shore orcs and their allies created there; Ephisis also named the Red Wind Corsairs as looters.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's herald suggested he could take a League city in recompense, and Ephisis cited the Wolves of War as looters and Sarvos as a city the Grendel might invade.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Cathan Canae's herald noted the Thule had already received a similar boon for fighting the Jotun and Druj.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's herald recalled his boons used to move things around in Urizen, and the conquest of Zenith was among those Cathan Canae will hear about.
n.Varushka: Sadogua is furious that the Circle of Zulgan-Tash moved the Whistling Strand to Varushka and suggested the Senate cede the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun, while Irra Harah barred any Varushkan from his parley.
n.Wintermark: Cathan Canae will grant a boon to two Wintermark warband leaders who fought Cold Sun at the beacons, and Ephisis offered Ogila's Tower in Kalpaheim, whose Merchant title could become a Wintermark national position.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Sadogua's herald idly imagined trapping the Castle of Thorns in an hourglass as one of several reprisals he chose not to pursue.
t.Bay of Catazar: Ephisis's proposed law against robbing Grendel property would ban Imperial privateering in the bay.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: as Grendel-held land it falls only within Ephisis's general discussion of conquering territory without looting it.
t.Hahnmark: Cathan Canae praised the Winterfolk victories at the beacons here and will grant a boon to the warrior who led their warband against Cold Sun in Hahnmark.
t.Kallavesa: Cathan Canae praised the Winterfolk victories at the beacons here and will grant a boon to the warrior who led their warband against Cold Sun in Kallavesa.
t.Madruga: Irra Harah had been aiding the Freeborn at Madruga, and Surut described the bitterness kindled there by the Broken Shore orcs and their allies as a conflagration hard to outmatch.
t.Ossium: The conquest of Ossium is among the triumphs the commended generals will present to Cathan Canae's castellan for the chance of the Fist of the Black Glacier boon.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Ephisis used a possible Grendel invasion of Sarvos to illustrate that conquest would still be allowed under her proposal, but not burning or looting.
t.Sermersuaq: The conquest of Sermersuaq is among the triumphs the commended generals will present to Cathan Canae's castellan for the chance of her boon.
t.Skallahn: Zakalwe's Polemarch marches with the Bloodcloaks in Skallahn, and Zakalwe wishes to discuss the invasion's timing and challenges with the Imperial Seer at the Spring Equinox.
t.The Barrens: Cathan Canae considers the matter of ceding Barrens land to the Spears of the Pines settled, while Irra Harah will parley only about events there, citing Dourfell Keep, the Black Wind and the Vendarri.
t.Zenith: The conquest of Zenith is among the triumphs the commended generals will present to Cathan Canae's castellan for the chance of her boon.

Between stone and salt.d: More than twenty-five thousand Imperial soldiers, joined by fey warriors of the Queen of the Pennants, invaded Mareave. The Brine Turtles and Salt Lord Ehsan's soldiers were badly outnumbered. Icarion fell, and the walled town of Rathmonna in Nadir held out for a fortnight. The defenders then rallied at the Gate of Storms in Eoradal, leaving the Empire a fifth of the way to taking that region. The Brine Turtles lost perhaps five for every Imperial casualty. The page also sets out opportunities for the coming battle: slaying drake warbeasts, bribing the Dracaild of Rathmonna and the Red Ibis, buying Sannite contracts, finding a map to Rucraic's Aerie, and hiring the Gaineamh Tine.

n.Grendel: The Grendel lost Icarion and Nadir, and the Brine Turtles suffered heavy casualties largely alone. Soldiers openly asked where the rest of the Grendel were, while locals voiced resentment at the Council that had sent no reinforcements.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun fought in the invasion, and some Sannites found lost family in Eoradal, with mixed results. There was friction with the Sunstorm over how to treat Mareave's orcs, and a deal was offered to free hundreds of enslaved orcs for the Sannite sept.
n.The League: The Towerjacks broke Rathmonna's walls and the Seventh Wave located the Gate of Storms, as the League went to war for the first time as five cities. Apulian's new orc citizens welcomed the armies warmly, and the Red Ibis offered paid intelligence.
n.Urizen: Many of the Imperial captains' warbands with the Golden Axe were Urizen, and some Urizen eagerly explored the Skouran ruins of conquered Mareave. Meanwhile Apulian's citizens feared the Urizen rebels in Ankra and Cinion.
n.Varushka: The Golden Axe led the invasion with almost seven thousand Varushkans, in the spirit of the Vard, and were the first to set foot in Mareave. Their general was offered the chance to hire the Gaineamh Tine to ransack the region.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the Winter Sun's general speaks only of striking the Grendel before they can set the Imperial coast ablaze.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the Towerjacks' engineers from Holberg drew interest in Apulian, and Holberger immigrants there spread fearful tales of the Blight.
t.Mareave: Imperial armies conquered the northern hills of Icarion and Nadir and made inroads into Eoradal. The Brine Turtles held out from the Gate of Storms, and the territory's free, independent orcs took to the hills.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the armies gathered at the Court of the White Fountain as guests of the sentinels before marching into Spiral.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvosi immigrants in Apulian fuelled local fears with stories of the Doom that befell their former homes.
t.Skarsind: A few orcs from Eoradal resolved to come north to Skarsind with Sannite relatives. A proposed deal with the North Mareave Trading Consortium could free hundreds more to join the Sannite sept there.
t.Spiral: The armies marched through Spiral under Screed's oppressive aura to Apulian, where citizens cheered them south while fearing Grendel reprisals and the Urizen rebels.

r.Mareave/Beoraidh: Mentioned in passing: the seat of Salt Lord Ehsan, whose garrison soldiers fought alongside the Brine Turtles but were disliked by the locals.
r.Mareave/Eoradal: The Empire is about a fifth of the way to conquering this ruin-strewn hill region, where the Brine Turtles hold the Gate of Storms. Slaying the Grendel drakes or finding a hidden map to the Aerie could tip the balance.
r.Mareave/Icarion: Icarion was the first region to fall, conquered by Imperial troops after the outnumbered defenders fell back, and some slaves were freed from its mines.
r.Mareave/Nadir: Nadir was conquered after Rathmonna fell to the Towerjacks within a fortnight. The Dracaild of Rathmonna now threatens to loose drakes on Imperial supply lines unless paid sixty thrones.
r.Spiral/Ankra: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's citizens feared what the Urizen rebels in Ankra might work against them.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Mentioned in passing: Apulian's citizens feared what the Urizen rebels in Cinion might work against them.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: the grim oppression emanating from Screed made the march miserable and tormented the soldiers' dreams.

Blue flowers in the snow.d: Most Empire-loyal Urizeni left Spiral for Zenith and Redoubt. The Senate passed Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian's motion spending 35 thrones a season on mana for Vale of Shadows over Urizen interests, meeting the demands of Actius of the Deathless Cave. Rebels under Tiborion and Caela still held Ankra and Cinion. Aurum's mandate warned that if any army moved against them before Autumn 386YE, all Urizen would rise. Tiborion sought a powerful political position, perhaps a national War Mage title. The League's Lorenzo's Legacies could be redirected to cut the cost, and an Urizen mandate could shape Apulian's culture. The Icy Maw curse halved mana in Morrow and Redoubt.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Dawn is cited as having held the War Mage title in recent memory.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are named among those whose attacks left Urizen exposed, and the curse does not appear to be their work.
n.Grendel: There is a feared but unproven danger that the rebel spires might reach a secret agreement with the Salt Lords. The Silent Bell or the Shuttered Lantern could investigate this.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr are cited as having held the War Mage title in recent memory.
n.The League: The League kept settling into Spiral, buying former spire buildings and calling with Urizen for Apulian to embrace Urizeni culture. It was offered the chance to redirect Lorenzo's Legacies to fund the shrouds, while some voices like Ludwig Bassilo von Temeschwar urged exploiting Spiral's resources.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Assembly backed the Spiral rebels, and Aurum's mandate threatens a nation-wide rising if the Empire sends troops against them. Meanwhile the Icy Maw curse on Morrow and Redoubt, blamed on another Imperial nation, deepened Urizeni resentment.

t.Holberg: Holberg's Legacy of Courage is one of four great works whose mana a Senate motion could redirect to shroud Spiral's spires, ending its extra mana for League sites.
t.Morrow: The Icy Maw curse halved mana production in Morrow and afflicted its magicians with malaise and ill temper. The Citadel Guard's arcane consolidation there yielded only half the expected crystals, and worse effects loom if the curse continues.
t.Redoubt: Departing Urizeni from Spiral founded new spires in Redoubt, which also suffered the Icy Maw curse that halved its mana sites. Worse effects loom if the curse is renewed.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's Legacy of Pride could have its mana redirected to Spiral under a Senate motion, as urged by Isaia Pavone di Sarvos.
t.Spiral: Spiral remained split: the League held most regions while rebel spires held Ankra and Cinion. The Senate funded Vale of Shadows over all Urizen interests there, which blocks other rituals on them and new mana-producing Senate projects in the territory.
t.Tassato: Tassato's Legacy of Ambition is one of the great works whose mana could be redirected to support Spiral's spires if the Senate so chose.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's Varushkan heritage was held up as a model for Apulian absorbing Urizeni culture. Its Legacy of Loyalty could be redirected to fund the Spiral shrouds.
t.Zenith: Urizeni loyal to the Empire left Spiral to establish new spires in Zenith, and the shrouds aim to keep Spiral's spires linked with those of Zenith.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Ankra remains under the control of the Urizen rebel spires.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Mentioned in passing: Apstrus is listed among the regions still controlled by the League.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus remains in League hands, and the former bishop Ludwig Bassilo von Temeschwar has newly arrived there calling for the exploitation of Spiral's resources.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Mentioned in passing: Ateri is listed among the regions still controlled by the League.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Cinion remains under the control of the Urizen rebel spires.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: Ossuary, home of the mithril mine, is listed among the regions still controlled by the League.
r.Spiral/Screed: Mentioned in passing: Screed is listed among the League-held regions, with the remark that the less said about it the better.

Bright yellow blooms.d: After meeting Heilyn Bronwen's Rest at the Summer Solstice, Gethyn Blood-And-Sweat's Rising Tide settled at the Spire of the Golden Wood, famed yellow dye-makers limited by scarce iridescent gloaming. They offered two opportunities. The Senate could commission the Gloaming Forum (12 white granite, 36 crowns, three months, a Bourse seat commission slot) near the spire, creating an Urizen national title, the Gloaming Merchant, chosen by Tally of the Votes, who could trade gloaming for pooled local weirwood and would be charged with improving Morrow's Prosperity. Separately, for the coming year the Mirrored Maschieri may buy one mask a season from the spire for gloaming; buying two or more would see the Tide seek to make the arrangement permanent.

n.Navarr: The Navarr Basilisk of the Bourse, Heilyn Bronwen's Rest, set the initiative in motion by asking the Rising Tide to draw up proposals for improving the Canterspire Circle.
n.Urizen: Urizen stands to gain a new national title, the Gloaming Merchant, chosen by its mana site owners, while the Spire of the Golden Wood and neighbouring spires could profit from trade in dyes, masks and weirwood despite tensions with the League.

t.Morrow: Morrow is the focus of the proposals: a possible Gloaming Forum near the Spire of the Golden Wood, whose Merchant would be bound to use weirwood for Morrow's Prosperity, and a mask trade bringing gloaming to its dye-makers.

r.Morrow/Operus: In Operus the Rising Tide met the Canterspire Circle's lumberjack crews without disrupting their work and took up residence at the Spire of the Golden Wood, where any forum would be built.

Broken sword.d: Herminius of the House of the Wanderer's mandate (284-10) shattered the Temple of the Four Winds. Unrepentant scholars renamed themselves the Disciples of Sulemaine and rejected the Assembly and the Arbiter, who lost their bounty of liao. Having reversed its 383YE praise of Sulemaine, the Assembly lost authority: Urizen congregations give 2 fewer votes and 1 fewer liao until Winter Solstice 386YE. The Assembly upheld a mandate, raised by Herminius and enacted by Clytemnestra, urging loyal scholars to carry Sulemaine's teachings across the Empire. There will be no new sword scholars in Urizen, and the last of them may found a sodality. Galene Netherwatch's judgement keeps Urizen bound only by greater-majority mandates.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the sword scholars' earlier links with the yeofolk of Dawn are cited as a step towards forming a sodality.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Sulemaine is recalled as having taken up the sword against the Highborn missionaries who came to Urizen.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Harwyn Eternal of the Navarr Assembly is named among those whose statements encouraged the departing sword scholars to settle in their lands.
n.The League: Departing sword scholars are expected to inspire the League's bravos to seek Wisdom, though the influence will be slow and subtle.
n.Urizen: Urizen loses its sword scholar tradition, sees its Assembly's authority and congregations weakened for a year, and is left with an abandoned Temple of the Four Winds and an Arbiter without a clear role.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the sword scholars' earlier links with the bravos of Holberg are cited as progress towards a sodality.
t.Zenith: The Disciples of Sulemaine have largely withdrawn to reclusive temples deep in Zenith's mountains, where a few vow revenge on those they feel betrayed Sulemaine.

Church of your heart.d: While the Granite Pillar defended the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion from the Winnowers, veterans awaited Synod confirmation before leaving their chapters. A Vigilance mandate costing 50 doses of liao would grant Highborn armies Bring Virtue to the Scions: more casualties inflicted on scions, more casualties suffered. A Loyalty mandate would grant Defence of the Virtuous: stronger defence against scions, at the same cost in casualties. Neither competes with the other. Enacting either would stop Highborn armies generating opportunities until every Cold Sun army in the Empire is destroyed. Kalina Jadwigowna Piosnkowa Prochnost and Sławomir Rabovich Bolotstrazh offered Varushkan versions using Partner of Greatness.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Assembly could send veterans to the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave and Valiant Pegasus, gaining offensive or defensive orders against the scions. The price would be that its armies generate no further opportunities until Cold Sun is driven from the Empire.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is named as one of the territories where scions caused suffering that the Loyal hope never to see repeated.
n.Varushka: Alternative mandates were offered to the Varushkan Assembly that would give its armies either new order, usable only in Varushkan territories. Enacting one would bar the Assembly from further mandates until the Cold Sun armies in Varushka are defeated.

t.Bastion: The Granite Pillar under General Asenath was defending the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion against the Winnowers, and the veterans' first aim was to make the Highborn homeland safe.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is cited as a territory where scion horrors befell civilians, a fate the Loyal want to prevent elsewhere.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Miaren is cited alongside Karov as a place where scions brought harm that Highborn dedicates of Loyalty vow will not be repeated.

r.Karov/Duzekani: Mentioned in passing: Sławomir's proposed Varushkan mandate declares that what happened in Livardz and Duzekani will not be repeated.

Construct A Fair Price.d: Announced by Groza, Legion Engineer, at the Winter Solstice 385YE, the commission cost 10 wains of weirwood, 30 crowns and standard costs, and took three months to build. Because the Legion Engineer could not amend a title to grant custodianship of a sinecure, the Senate voted at the Summer Solstice 386YE to amend the Champion of Prosperity title to include it. Funding came in instalments from Serenus Starsong, Rhys Nighthaven, Thiaga i Pérez i Riqueza, Tethros i Zuhri i Erigo and finally Bartimaeus, who supplied the remaining money and the weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. Once complete, the Champion of Prosperity was to receive 216 rings each season from the Spring Equinox 387YE.

n.Urizen: The new sinecure was built on Urizen land in Zenith, bringing a farm and a seasonal income to an Imperial title within the nation's territory.

t.Zenith: Zenith gained a new farm sinecure, 'A Fair Price', which yields 216 rings each season for the Champion of Prosperity from the Spring Equinox 387YE.

r.Zenith/Iteri: Iteri was chosen as the site of 'A Fair Price', a farm sinecure attached to the Champion of Prosperity and completed after funding finished in late 386YE.

Construct Garden City in Holberg.d: Passed in Winter 385YE, the motion was run as a disbursement with increasing numbers of commissions, since the project needed four commissions over a year. It passed at one commission, costing 50 thrones and taking twelve months. Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, as Master of the Koboldi, announced support at the Spring Equinox 386YE, and Gustavus Tolski van Temeschwar, as Chair of the Wolf, did so at the Summer Solstice and Autumn Equinox 386YE. Many citizens, largely of Holberg, donated thrones and crowns towards it across 385YE and 386YE. On completion, Holmauer became a garden city and gained the Uplifting quality.

n.The League: The League's Senator for Holberg proposed the motion, and League citizens, many bearing the name van or von Holberg, provided much of the money that brought the City of Flowers to completion.

t.Holberg: Holberg's capital was remade as the City of Flowers, a year-long folly that Holberg's own citizens largely paid for.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer was transformed into a garden city and gained the Uplifting quality once the construction was complete.

Construct Hall of Rund.d: Proposed by the senator for Kallavesa and seconded by Kahraman, the motion took up the opportunity presented by the Old Ways Wind of Fortune. The Hall of Rund is a sinecure that produces liao, and its holder, the Speaker of the Crows, is to lead and guide Wintermark's National Assembly. Construction required 10 wains of weirwood, 6 wains of white granite and 48 crowns, and took three months. After the Winter Solstice, Veikko Bondforger supplied the weirwood and white granite, and Gisli i Phovas i Guerra provided 6 thrones. With the work complete, the National Assembly of Wintermark can appoint the first Speaker of the Crows at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gains a new national position, the Speaker of the Crows, appointed by and charged with leading and guiding its National Assembly. The Assembly can make its first appointment at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

t.Kallavesa: The Hall of Rund was built at Rundhal in Kallavesa as a liao-giving sinecure, on a motion proposed by Kallavesa's own senator.

Construct Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mem.d: As part of completing the restoration of Holmauer Park, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund used his Imperial Wayleave to announce that the entrepreneurial souvenir stall run by Claude of Holberg, formerly known as 'The Rickety Stall', would become a standard business sinecure. The Kleists of Holberg invested coin and wains in the work. The project cost 5 thrones, beyond the costs set by the opportunity, and took three months to complete. Lula Kleist von Ennerlund provided the 5 thrones after the Winter Solstice 385YE. With the work complete, the title of Financier of Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes can now be appointed by unanimous decision of the League's senators.

n.The League: The League's senators gained a new business title to award, the Financier of Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes, which they must appoint by unanimous decision.

t.Holberg: Holberg gained a new business sinecure, built through investment by the Kleists of Holberg as part of the restoration of Holmauer Park.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: In Holmauer Park, Claude of Holberg's makeshift Rickety Stall was turned into the established souvenir business Holberg's Phantasmagorical Mementoes, completing the park's restoration.

Construct House of Illumination and Ligh.d: Announced by Dima Vasilyevna Novosad, Master of the Koboldi, the commission followed the Out of the Abyss wind of fortune. It created two sinecures: the Architect of Illumination and the Merchant Boyar of the Light Market. It cost 75 wains of white granite and 225 crowns and took six months to build. Bledri and Siân of the Eternal Family in Navarr were thanked for pledging 10 wains. Many citizens gave crowns, thrones and granite between Winter 385YE and Autumn 387YE. Once complete, both titles became available for election for the first time at the Winter Solstice 387YE.

n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Bledri and Siân of the Eternal Family in Navarr were thanked for pledging 10 wains towards the construction.
n.Urizen: Urizen gained the Architect of Illumination, a new title in Redoubt to be elected by a tally of the votes of Urizen mana site owners, first at the Winter Solstice 387YE.
n.Varushka: A commission announced by Varushka's Master of the Koboldi and largely funded by Varushkan donors gave the nation the Merchant Boyar of the Light Market, elected by Varushkan forest and mine owners, with a shortened first term of three seasons.

t.Miekarova: The Light Market was built in Essk, Miekarova, and is the seat of the new Merchant Boyar of the Light Market title.
t.Redoubt: The House of Illumination was built in Cargo, Redoubt, and is the seat of the new Architect of Illumination title.

Construct Leshun Market.d: The Leshun Market was announced by the Boyar of the Iron Roads rather than through a vote. It cost 16 wains of weirwood and 3 thrones and took three months to build. Funding came from several donors after the Winter Solstice 385YE: Druhain Olodniky gave a wain of weirwood, Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn gave 2 thrones, 6 crowns and 17 rings, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave a crown, and others gave small sums. Pavel Novak supplied the remaining 15 wains of weirwood after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. With the work complete, the new Speaker to the Leshun would be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE by Tally of the Votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners.

n.Varushka: Varushkan citizens, led by the Boyar of the Iron Roads, paid for the market, and the Varushkan mine and forest owners gained the right to choose the new Speaker to the Leshun.

t.Karsk: The Leshun Market was built in Karsk, giving the territory a new ministry whose Speaker to the Leshun would first be appointed at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

Construct Ministry for Bursar of the Con.d: The commission was announced by Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad as Arcane Architect. It cost 12 wains of mithril and 36 crowns and would take three months to build in Moresvah, Karsk. Novosad supplied 7 wains of mithril and 4 thrones 4 crowns after the Winter Solstice 385YE. Otmar van Holberg provided the remaining 5 wains of mithril after the Autumn Equinox 386YE. With the work finished, the Bursar of the Conclave could purchase mana crystals at the standard costs.

n.Varushka: The Bursar of the Conclave's improved ministry was built on Varushkan soil in Karsk, and a Varushkan-named Arcane Architect, Aleksandr Zoravich Novosad, announced it and provided most of the funding.

t.Karsk: Karsk was chosen as the site of the ministry, which was completed after mithril was supplied in 385YE and 386YE.

r.Karsk/Moresvah: The ministry allowing the Bursar of the Conclave to buy mana crystals at standard costs was constructed in Moresvah.

Construct Office of the Lantern Wolf.d: The commission created a sinecure in Tassato Regario, as described in the Battle cries Wind of Fortune. Besides the standard costs it required 10 wains of weirwood, 10 wains of white granite and 60 crowns, and three months to complete. Ikelos Moretti supplied much of the weirwood and white granite. Gianluca Di Zobbras, Rhys Nighthaven, Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov, Farren Silver Streams, Fintan Nighthaven and others contributed money. Katarina van Palantíri's large donation of money, weirwood and granite after the Autumn Equinox 386YE helped finish it. Once the work was complete, the Lantern Wolf became available for the League's National Assembly to elect as a yearly appointment, for the first time at the Winter Solstice 386YE.

n.The League: The League gained a new national position, the Lantern Wolf, which its National Assembly could elect each year from the Winter Solstice 386YE.

t.Tassato: The Office of the Lantern Wolf was raised within the walls of Tassato, giving the League territory a new sinecure.

r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Tassato Regario became the site of the new Office of the Lantern Wolf, built with weirwood and white granite.

Construct Reikos Counting House.d: Proposed by the senator for Reikos and seconded by Casinea, the motion took up an opportunity from the Forwards and Rewards Wind of Fortune. It cost seven wains of white granite, seven wains of weirwood and 42 crowns, with three months to build, and was to be fully funded by Highguard benefactors. Rhesa provided 5 thrones 1 crown and all the materials, and Septus Sentinels Tower gave the final crown. Once complete, the Benefactor of High Chalcis was first appointable by the Highguard National Assembly at the Spring Equinox 386YE, and from the Summer Solstice 386YE the Virtue Fund receives 10 crowns each summit from Reikos citizens.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a new national title, the Benefactor of High Chalcis, appointed by its National Assembly from Spring 386YE, and Highguard benefactors such as Rhesa and Septus Sentinels Tower paid for the whole construction.

t.Reikos: A prosperous counting house was built in Reikos to oversee the Gardens of High Chalcis, and its citizens now donate 10 crowns each summit to the Virtue Fund from Summer 386YE.

Construct Semmerholm Counting House.d: The commission cost 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, and was due to take three months. Funding arrived slowly through donations from Winter Solstice 385YE to Autumn Equinox 386YE. Amicia of the Semmerlak gave the most, including a throne, crowns, all five wains of weirwood and all five of white granite. Gianluca Di Zobbras, Kostjya, Berith Relieur, Triska Markova, Rhys Nighthaven and Bertrand Gardener also gave money, and there were small anonymous donations. Once the work was complete, citizens of Semmerholm began donating 11 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

n.Dawn: Semmerholm's senator proposed the motion, and Dawnish donors led by Amicia of the Semmerlak supplied most of the money and all of the materials for the counting house.

t.Semmerholm: A Prosperous Counting House was built in Semmerholm, and the territory's citizens now donate 11 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Construct Spider's Dream Bridge.d: Proposed by the Senator for Necropolis and seconded by Segura, the motion originally called for the bridge to be rebuilt with an additional white granite fortification. It passed at 240 thrones, which were disbursed to the Senator for Necropolis, but it was amended later in the season to remove the fortification. Construction needed 30 wains of mithril, 10 wains of white granite, 15 thrones in labour and three months. After the Winter Solstice, Eli of the Cenotaph supplied 15 wains of mithril, 15 thrones and the white granite, and Giacomo Corvinoscuro supplied the remaining 15 wains of mithril. With the bridge complete, rapid army movement was restored and the Spider's Tollkeep again received its seasonal income of two thrones.

n.The Brass Coast: The restored bridge reopened a quick route for Imperial armies into and out of the Brass Coast's territory of Madruga, and the motion was seconded by the Senator for Segura.
n.The League: The League's territories of Sarvos and Tassato regained fast military links to Madruga, and the motion was proposed by the Senator for Necropolis, who received the 240 thrones.

t.Madruga: Imperial armies could once again march quickly between Madruga and the League territories of Sarvos and Tassato.
t.Sarvos: Once the repairs were complete, Imperial armies could again move swiftly from Sarvos to Madruga and back.
t.Tassato: The rebuilt bridge restored a quick route for Imperial armies between Tassato and Madruga.

Construct Spy Network in Reinos.d: Bernard Dugdale, the Imperial Spymaster, announced in Winter 385YE that a spy network would be built in Reinos. He framed it as an act of loyalty to the General of the Red Wind Corsairs, honouring a previous agreement, and as a step towards hamstringing the Lasambrians and ending the western front. The work required 10 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns and was to take three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice Dugdale himself provided 3 thrones 6 crowns and the weirwood. Once finished, military units would be able to support the network to uncover information about Reinos.

n.Jotun: The Empire moved to gather intelligence on Jotun-held Reinos, with the stated aim of weakening the Lasambrian Jotun and bringing the war with them to a close.

t.Reinos: A new Imperial spy network was commissioned in Jotun-held Reinos. Once complete, military units could support it to uncover information about the territory.

Construct Tassato Counting House.d: The motion was proposed by the Conscience of the Senate and seconded by the senator for Tassato. It disbursed funds for a Counting House costing 5 wains of weirwood, 5 wains of white granite and 30 crowns, with three months needed to complete it. Gianluca Di Zobbras and Richardo Glostari di Sarvos each provided a crown after the Winter Solstice 385YE. After the Spring Equinox 386YE, Virgil Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato provided 3 thrones 4 crowns along with the full weirwood and white granite. Once the work is complete, citizens of the territory will donate 16 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

n.The League: League citizens funded the folly, most of all Virgil Sanguineo Rezia di Tassato, who supplied the weirwood, white granite and most of the money. Tassato's senator seconded the motion.

t.Tassato: A Counting House is to be built in Tassato. Once it is complete, the territory's citizens will donate 16 crowns to the Virtue Fund each summit.

Construct The Gloaming Forum.d: Zorya (Zosia) Swietoslawa Przewalski, Bearer of an Imperial Wayleave, announced the construction. The Gloaming Merchant may purchase weirwood under the opportunity presented by the Basilisk of the Bourse and the Spire of Golden Wood. The work costs 12 wains of white granite and 36 crowns, plus the costs set by the opportunity, and takes three months. After the Winter Solstice 385YE, Edmundo of Damakan's forge provided 4 thrones 4 crowns and 6 wains of white granite, and Spyridonakes of the Lighthouse-That-Was provided a further 6 wains. Once the work is complete, the Gloaming Merchant will be chosen by Tally of the Votes of Urizen's mana site owners.

n.Urizen: Urizen gains a new national position, the Gloaming Merchant, with access to weirwood. It will be chosen by Tally of the Votes of the nation's mana site owners once the Gloaming Forum is complete.

t.Morrow: The Gloaming Forum is being built in Morrow, giving the territory a bourse seat that trades in weirwood.

r.Morrow/Operus: Operus is the site of the new Gloaming Forum ministry, which was funded with white granite and crowns after the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Construct Three Hands' Stand.d: The commission, announced by Laughlan Vi Temeschwar as Master of Rings, followed the opportunity described in The greatest city in the world wind of fortune. It cost 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns, on top of the cost set by the opportunity, and took three months to complete. After the Winter Solstice the materials were provided in equal shares by Giacomo Corvinoscuro, Claus Friedrich von Holberg, Gancio di Catazar, Laughlan Vi Temeschwar and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund, each giving 4 wains of mithril and 1 throne 4 crowns. With the work complete, the Red-Eyed Reaper was to be auctioned as a League national bourse seat for the first time at the Spring Equinox 386YE, for a reduced term.

n.The League: The League gains a new national bourse seat producing weirwood, the Red-Eyed Reaper of Three Hands' Stand, to be first auctioned among its citizens at the Spring Equinox 386YE for a reduced term.

t.Holberg: Three Hands' Stand was built in Holberg at the request of the Sand Fishers, giving the territory a new weirwood-producing bourse seat.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Laughlan Vi Temeschwar, whose name refers to the territory, announced the commission as Master of Rings and contributed materials to it.

Construct the Phoenix Flame.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by Astolat, the motion commissioned the Phoenix Flame in Astolat, Dawn, at a cost of 30 wains of mithril, 30 wains of white granite and 180 crowns. It would take six months to complete. Once built, it was to be ceded to Meraud. Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés provided most of the materials and money after the Winter Solstice 385YE and the Spring Equinox 386YE. Smaller crown donations came from Serenus Starsong, Rhys Nighthaven, Ser Lucan Mortére and Aramis du Froste. Once the work was complete, the Tender of the Phoenix Flame could be appointed by Declaration of Candidacy.

n.Dawn: Dawn gained a new sinecure in one of its territories, with a new Imperial title, the Tender of the Phoenix Flame, to be appointed by Declaration of Candidacy. Dawnish donors such as Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés bore most of the cost.

t.Astolat: The Phoenix Flame was built in Astolat over six months and ceded to Meraud once complete. Astolat's senator seconded the motion.

Despise treachery.d: Acting on Senator Lizzie Stamp's motion, the magistrates searched every household in Bregasland. House Brawness resisted arrest and was executed for treason. The Droverbill Clan were only fined for handling stolen goods. Three dozen Clakes were executed, but Sammy Clake escaped to Sallow with a five-throne bounty on his head. More than a score of other traitors were executed and dozens fined. House Greywater, unrewarded for opposing the Fishers, grew bitter. The North Fens became rebellious, the Grey Fens sullen and the Rushes resentful. The Assembly of Loyalty faced a choice over recognising Bushel Sykes. The Jotun carried the dying Mathilda Fisher to the Wintermark camp, and she asked to be buried at Fisher's Rock.

n.Jotun: Jotun warriors kept their word after losing the battle of champions and bore Mathilda Fisher, whom they honour as a jarl, to Anvil under a flag of truce. They intend to witness how the Empire treats her death and burial, and to report it to the other jarls.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly backed the magistrates' purge of Bregasland and recognised Bushel Sykes' Loyalty. Many Bregas Marchers were executed or fined, and lasting grudges now fester among Marcher households.
n.Wintermark: Iron Osric was asked to supply an honour guard of Wintermark warriors to escort the dying Mathilda Fisher. The Jotun will deliver her into the Wintermark camp at Anvil, where Jarl Igya has asked that she be allowed to die with honour.

t.Bregasland: Magistrates searched every farm and settlement, executing and fining collaborators. The territory is stable for now but scarred by sullen, resentful, embittered and rebellious regions. Burying Fisher there would leave the whole territory embittered.
t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun had threatened to spirit Mathilda Fisher away to Fjorknae had the Empire lost the battle of champions.
t.Tromsa: The Empire's invasion of Tromsa led to Fisher's mortal wounding at the Battle of Viheltavathorn and her surrender after a battle of champions at Oksenesfestsal. Returning her body to Tromsa for burial is one option being weighed.

r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Mentioned in passing: Gravenmarch is noted as home to many Marchers who remain loyal to the Empire.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Droverbill Clan escaped with heavy fines for profiteering and handling stolen goods. Anger that they got off lightly has left the region sullen, which would raise army upkeep costs if the mood spreads.
r.Bregasland/North Fens: House Brawness was all but destroyed after battling the magistrates, leaving the region rebellious. The unrewarded House Greywater has also made it embittered.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: Bushel Sykes, who died at the Wet Dog tavern in Ottery, came from here. If the Assembly of Loyalty recognises his Virtue, the North Fens' rebellious mood will spread to Ottermire.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: Three dozen Clakes of Beandown were executed and others fined into poverty, while Sammy Clake went to ground in Sallow. The region is now resentful and hungry for payback.

Dreaming in strands.d: The bridge, badly damaged in a raid before the Summer Solstice 385YE, blocks armies moving between Madruga and Sarvos or Tassato, cuts off refugees fleeing the Grendel and halts southern trade and the Tollkeep's tolls. With plans obtained from the Sarvosi engineer Margueritte, repair would cost 30 mithril, 10 white granite and 120 crowns. Optional additions were Tall Hal's barbican fortifications, a Trivento merchants' quarter creating the Ostiary of Trivento ministry, a great work wharf at Vassa's Eye boosting Madruga fleets, and Emperor Giovanni's plan to pay the Tollkeep five thrones per army crossing. All depend on the bridge being restored, and the Grendel threat to Madruga makes construction risky without an army to protect it.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: a Highborn magistrate eyes Eilian as though he might be a Druj assassin in disguise.
n.Grendel: The Grendel invasion of Madruga threatens any rebuilding. If they captured Torres or Bocche, work would become impossible and all materials would be lost. The page also recalls their failed attempt to destroy the bridge in Spring 380YE.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highguard journals were among Margueritte's sources, and a historical senator for Necropolis led the opposition to Giovanni's toll plan.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Emperor Ahraz's preoccupation with the Orc Rebellion is given as the reason Concetta di Trivento's proposals failed.
n.Jotun: The page credits a Jotun raid with badly damaging the bridge. Liathaven, then in Jotun hands, would only gain a Trivento-linked title if conquered.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn have lost a major trade route and refugees cannot reach the League. A proposed Vassa's Eye wharf would boost Madruga fleets and could create a Freeborn Harbourmaster position, alongside a possible Caravan Master of the Sunset Road in Calvos.
n.The League: The Sarvosi Tollkeep has lost toll income and could gain five thrones per army crossing under Giovanni's plan. Trivento could become a trade hub with a new League title, the Ostiary of Trivento.
n.The Marches: Marchers could gain a Bailiff of Sarcombe Market if a later great work boosted Mournwold farms after the Gateway to the South was built. The fortification plans were drawn up by Tall Hal, a yeofolk architect from Odd's End.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bridge plays an important but limited role in supporting Bay of Catazar trade routes.
t.Kahraman: Kahraman is linked to Trivento by river under the proposed trade network, and a future great work boosting its mines could create a Mistress of the Bounteous Parador at Nestor's Bounty. Recent events there are cited as a warning about building under barbarian threat.
t.Liathaven: The rivers would link Liathaven to Trivento. A boost to its forests could create a similar trade title, though only if the Jotun-held territory were conquered.
t.Madruga: Madruga is cut off from Imperial armies by the broken bridge and is not in Imperial hands amid the Grendel invasion. It stands to gain restored access, a fleet-boosting wharf at Vassa's Eye and a possible Caravan Master in Calvos.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the architect of the old fortification plans, Tall Hal, was a yeofolk from Odd's End.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold is linked to Trivento by river. A future great work boosting its farms could create the Bailiff of Sarcombe Market, a rival to Meade's Grand Market.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: a historical senator for Necropolis led the opposition that defeated Emperor Giovanni's toll plan.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos holds the northern end of the bridge and its Tollkeep, who would regain toll income from the repair. Neighbouring Trivento could be expanded into a trade hub to rival Sarvos.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Torfast trading post is cited as the anchor of the Northern trade network that a southern equivalent might imitate.
t.Tassato: The damaged bridge impedes armies moving between Tassato and Madruga. Tassato would be reached by river trade from an expanded Trivento.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Mentioned in passing: the page refers to Kahraman's mines and a proposed title at Nestor's Bounty but does not name the Jade Range.
r.Madruga/Torres: Torres's capture by enemies would make the repair impossible and forfeit all materials contributed. If the bridge were fortified, holding Torres would preserve military control of the bridge and allow a beachhead across the river.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: Bocche anchors the bridge's northern side. Losing it would halt repairs, while holding it would keep control of a fortified bridge and allow invasion of Torres beyond the usual beachhead limit.
r.Skarsind/Southpine: Mentioned in passing: the trading post at Torfast is held up as the model for a southern trade network.

Excavate Holberg Embankment.d: The motion sought the Senate's permission to dig a deep embankment before the Walls of Holberg. It stated that the work needed no commission and would not raise the upkeep of the walls. It cost 500 thrones and was to take twelve months to build. The motion passed. Funding came from many individual citizens between Winter 385YE and Summer 387YE. The largest donors were Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund, with Morgan Townsend von Holberg giving 100 thrones in Summer 387YE. Once finished, the Walls of Holberg will become a rank 6 fortification.

n.The League: The League's great city gained Senate approval to strengthen its defences, and many League citizens, especially of Holberg, paid for the work out of their own purses.

t.Holberg: A deep embankment is to be excavated before the Walls of Holberg, raising them to a rank 6 fortification once complete, with no increase in their upkeep.

Fading like a Flower.d: Madruga had already fallen to Grendel and Asavean invaders. Blightheart gained the blighted quality: no army can conquer it, and nothing lives there. The Spring rains holding the blight back are fading, and they cannot easily be renewed with Madruga cut off from the Imperial regio. Of four Dry Patricians seen entering the blight in Summer, three emerged in bone-white robes bearing the runes Yoorn, Hunger and Wisdom, leading cadres poised to advance when the rains stop. Options included Conclave orders investigating or seeking foreign aid, a Senate appraisal, a Silent Bell investigation, defensive armies, a rescue of captured Thule observers, and even giving the Grendel a Spring ritual.

n.Grendel: Grendel raiders captured Thule observers and are taking them towards the ruins of Siroc. The page floated a risky, possibly treasonous plan to give a Grendel coven such as Saltbinder Grekodh's the ritual Regrow the Land's Heart, since they control Madruga's Spring regio.
n.Highguard: The Freeborn di Tutamen family behind the blight has an unresolved historical link to the Highborn of Casinea and to Syrene's Wisdom. Wintergard magisters sought a midnight meeting with Highguard magisters in the Highguard chapel to share secrets.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Lasambrian Jotun's invasion of Kahraman is listed among the threats besetting the Brass Coast.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn lost the Great Grasses to the blight. Harbingers now threaten Segura and Kahraman, and hakima led by Ishala i Erigo called a council at Anvil with the Hakima of Salt and Sand to address the blight and the Coast's wider hardships.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Grendel magicians' earlier offer to cooperate against the horror in Spiral is cited as a precedent.
n.Thule: Thule warlocks investigating the blight were attacked by Grendel raiders, and at least two survivors are being taken towards Siroc. A rescue through the Sentinel Gate, needing The Cuckoo's Egg ritual, was proposed under the Ambassador to Otkodov.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Lutomysla Niegoslava, a cabalist from Karov, is one of the civil servants the Senate could choose for an appraisal of the blight.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the bay's surf is recalled as the place the nomads of the Great Grasses once brought their herds down towards.
t.Casinea: A cursed survivor of the blight has wandered Casinea begging for water, food and mana crystals amid rumours, though he appears human and is not spreading the blight. The Highborn of Casinea are historically linked to the di Tutamen.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Rahab still occupies Feroz, and Saltbinder Grekodh's Grendel coven on the Isle of Osseini is suggested as a possible recipient of a Spring ritual.
t.Kahraman: A third Harbinger, bearing the Rune of Wisdom, leads Dry Patricians and Parched gathered south of Nestor's Bounty, while the Lasambrian Jotun also invade the territory.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the cabalist Lutomysla Niegoslava, a possible appraiser for the Senate, hails from Karov.
t.Madruga: With the territory overrun by the Grendel and Siroc burned, the Great Grasses became Blightheart, a blighted region no army can conquer. The Spring rains protecting the rest of Madruga are fading.
t.Otkodov: Warlocks from Otkodov had gone to study the blight with a Dragon's interest; survivors have been captured by Grendel. Otkodov is also suggested as a place where the Celestial Arch might seek help.
t.Segura: Two Harbinger-led gatherings of Dry Patricians and Parched have massed on Segura's borders, held back only by the last Spring rains, while the Cold Sun's forces also contend in the territory.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: Grendel magicians once sought to cooperate with Imperial peers to contain the horror in Spiral, a precedent for the proposed approach.

r.Kahraman/Jade Range: A cadre of Dry Patricians and Parched gathered south of Nestor's Bounty, led by a bone-robed Harbinger marked with the Rune of Wisdom.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: A Harbinger bearing the Rune of Hunger leads a crowd of the blightbound massed across the bridge west of Cerevado, waiting for the rains to end.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The first Harbinger, bearing the glittering rune Yoorn, was seen at sunset along the edge of the Sobral Grasses with several dozen Dry Patricians and Parched.

Forwards and Rewards.d: Dialogos proposed Prosperous Counting Houses, each costing 5 weirwood, 5 white granite and 30 crowns, to gather donations for the Virtue fund. They would yield 10 to 16 crowns a season in thirteen listed territories. Haravgi established that fines had been kept by magistrates only by tradition. Gerard La Salle accepted that they belong in the treasury, and the Constitutional Court ruled that the Senate could send them to the Virtue fund. Haravgi offered a Virtue Assembly mandate withdrawing labour from the Senate until it does so. Velko Perunovich Razoradze offered a rival General Assembly mandate demanding the fines return to the magistrates. Other proposals were the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, the Benefactor of High Chalcis, a Mitwold statue and a Mistress of Monuments title.

n.Dawn: A counting house in Semmerholm could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
n.Highguard: Jemimah of Chalcis Ford proposed the Benefactor of High Chalcis, chosen by the Highborn Assembly and given herbs to heal the virtuous. The title could also redirect the Gardens' bounty by Senate announcement if created by Senate motion. A counting house in Reikos could add 10 crowns a season.
n.Imperial Orcs: A counting house in Skarsind could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
n.Navarr: A counting house in Miaren could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
n.The Brass Coast: A counting house in Segura could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
n.The League: The League's wealthy territories topped Dialogos' list, with counting houses in Tassato, Holberg, Sarvos and Temeschwar yielding 14 to 16 crowns each a season.
n.The Marches: The Marcher Assembly exalted Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft for warning of Siakha's heralds. Mitwolders then proposed a statue of him at Wayford that would also remember the Wayford Wanderers and some thirty people killed by the heralds.
n.Urizen: Urizeni priests Dialogos and Haravgi drove the Virtue fund proposals. Dialogos also proposed the Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade, a Urizen Assembly appointment that would use herbs and potions from Zenith to win friends for Urizen across the Empire.
n.Varushka: The boyars were formally thanked by the Urizen Assembly for providing the wayleave for the Gardens of Pallas. Velko Perunovich Razoradze proposed a rival mandate to return fines to the magistrates. Without a greater majority, that mandate would still allow commissions in Varushkan territories and leave the Boyar of the Iron Roads unaffected. A counting house in Karsk could add 12 crowns a season.
n.Wintermark: A counting house in Hahnmark could add 11 crowns a season, while Sermersuaq was cited as a place where donations would be far smaller.

t.Hahnmark: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Holberg: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 15 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Karsk: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 12 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Miaren: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Mitwold: A Statue of the Cockscroft Lad was proposed at Wayford, commemorating the warning against Siakha's heralds and those they killed. A counting house here could also add 12 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Reikos: Reikos citizens would fund the proposed Benefactor of High Chalcis with 7 each of five herbs a season, from offices beside the Gardens of High Chalcis. A counting house here could add 10 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Sarvos: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 14 crowns a season, its wealthy merchants making it one of the most lucrative sites.
t.Segura: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Semmerholm: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 11 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of where a counting house would draw far fewer donations than one in Sarvos.
t.Skarsind: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 13 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Tassato: Tassato was the most lucrative site on the list, where a counting house could add 16 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Temeschwar: A Prosperous Counting House here could add 14 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Jonathan Piper of Cockscroft, honoured by the proposed Mitwold statue, is noted to be an Upwolder.
t.Zenith: The Golden Cascade has boosted Zenith's farms and herb gardens, and its citizens would fund the proposed Beneficiary of the Golden Cascade from an enlarged counting house. That house would provide 10 crowns a season to the Virtue fund.

r.Mitwold/Maiden Downs: The proposed Statue of the Cockscroft Lad would stand at the old Wayford Wanderers practice ground in Wayford, costing 5 white granite and 15 crowns.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Mentioned in passing: the City of Sarvos in Cigno was cited as an especially wealthy place where a counting house would gather far more donations.

Hear your footsteps.d: Preceptor Malachai complained that finding lost objects is not the sodality's calling. Its agents confirmed the bell was probably an artefact, lost when Agramant-inspired sorcerers killed Friar Jillian Bevan at an old tower near King's Stoke. They linked the theft to the Circle of the Stones, a Marcher coven destroyed in Ashill in 346YE. The bell may lie in those ruins or with the raiders who destroyed the coven. They found no obvious Agramant cults in the Marches. They described three kinds of cult (pawns, fools and malefactors), warned about other Winter eternals, and suggested pursuing Kaarina White-Eye or Wemba the Bloody. Three mandates were proposed: two for the Wintermark assembly and one for the General Assembly.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: an investigator grumbles about trouble in Madruga that is not the Grendel's doing, and about Grendel spy rings.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the investigator Ziri is Highborn, and the Silent Bell note that the Highborn have always regarded the Winter eternals as monsters.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell speculate that whoever destroyed the Meeting Place in Sermersuaq was a 'fool' serving Agramant to make peace with the Jotun impossible.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: some of the Brass Coast are unhappy that their Prosperity was gifted to the eternal Tharim, a concern echoed by the Wisdom judgement.
n.The League: The investigation uncovered League history: the Circle of the Stones had cursed League cities, and its accuser Paulus Magen di Sarvos and his coven, the Childer of the Black Drop, were later declared sorcerers themselves.
n.The Marches: The bell was a Marcher relic held by the Threshers of Upwold, and the Silent Bell traced its theft to the Marcher coven Circle of the Stones, while finding no obvious signs of Agramant cults in the Marches today.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule is not named, though it holds part of Sermersuaq, where the remaining Agramant cult leaders are at large.
n.Urizen: The Wisdom judgement came from the Urizeni Ourania Neofoti, which lent it weight because many see Urizen as quick to accept eternal bargains. The proposed General Assembly mandate would have little effect on Urizen unless it passed with a greater majority.
n.Varushka: The page recalls that the Varushkan assembly had urged its people to make deals with dark powers, and notes that the proposed caution mandate would not affect Varushka without a greater majority.
n.Wintermark: The Wintermark assembly could pass mandates urging its people to support one another through a harsh winter or to fight the monsters threatening the whole nation. Either mandate would reward units that hunt in the Suaq Wastes or fight these threats and penalise those that do not.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Silent Bell's preceptor, Malachai, is from Casca's Doom.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the scions of Cold Sun remaining here are cited as one reason for the nationwide Wintermark mandate.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the scions of Cold Sun are still here, one of the threats cited in the nationwide Wintermark mandate.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: an investigator refers to unexplained trouble in Madruga beyond the Grendel.
t.Sermersuaq: Facing a harsh winter, with three Agramant cult leaders still at large, Sermersuaq could be rallied by a Wintermark mandate. It would ensure no settlement goes hungry, strengthen farms, and make it nearly impossible for Blood-on-the-Snow to win support here throughout 386YE.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: a Silent Bell agent posed as a League merchant from Tassato while visiting King's Stoke.
t.Upwold: The Silent Bell searched King's Stoke for the bell lost there in 290YE. Without finding it, they reconstructed the story of the haunting, the sorcerers' attack and the deaths of Friar Bevan and Creg Watcher.

r.Casinea/Casfall: Mentioned in passing: Preceptor Malachai of the Silent Bell is from Casca's Doom.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the cult leader Maarik the Golden Tongued is out of the Silent Bell's reach in the Silver Peaks.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Under either proposed Wintermark mandate, units that hunt in the Suaq Wastes would gain strength rather than suffer a penalty.
r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Mentioned in passing: Ashill, where the Circle of the Stones made its last stand and where the bell may still lie, is named but not placed in any region.
r.Upwold/The Heath: Mentioned in passing: the relic's legend begins with Brian of Heathford, who drove a ghost back into the Labyrinth with three days of rough music.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Mentioned in passing: neither King's Stoke, the ruined tower nor the Sign of the Tower inn where the investigators searched is placed in any region.

I remember you.d: Evander Slak announced what is probably his last Axou drug-selling visit, accompanied by the cambion Ilarch Kyther Deianeira. The theologian Theodosia of Ipotavo, believed to hold the Shield of Vigilance Bawn-watch, returned to Anvil. Endric of Lepidus found three lyric-only songs possibly by Elayne Silverlark and invited songsmiths to set them. Iosif Kosta brought Caoimhe Tend-Fallen a report on a Commonwealth aura. Annukka Juhaling came to warn of astronomancy's dangers. Cassius, a shattered stargazer, preached doom on the road. The sick herald Archipelago the Rising Leviathan sought healers. Thule merchants of the Five Fang Consortium sought investment. The Charnel Lord welcomed a Varushkan Empress and promised an unspecified gift.

n.Dawn: One of the three lost Silverlark songs appears to adapt a Dawnish original, and Dawnish troubadours are among those invited to compose a tune for its lyrics.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the stargazer Cassius was left shattered after escaping when the Druj took his spire, the Arch of the Sky.
n.Highguard: The Highborn poet Endric of Lepidus found the lost Silverlark songs, one adapted from a Highborn original, and hopes to publish the best arrangements for pilgrims of Loyalty.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the visiting Thule merchants planned to head first to the Imperial Orcs camp on arrival.
n.Thule: Merchants of the Five Fang Consortium, turned back twice before by heat and weather, came seeking Imperial investment in a scheme in Otkodov, though why they were not seeking it from fellow Thule was unclear.
n.Urizen: Cassius, a grief-stricken stargazer from the fallen Arch of the Sky, left his refuge in Morrow and walked to Anvil preaching visions of doom, apparently bound for the Brass Coast camp.
n.Varushka: The Charnel Lord of Branoc welcomed Varushka's return to the throne and promised Empress Vesna Borkovna Prochnost a gift, while the Varushkan merchant Iosif Kosta brought the Synod a report from the Commonwealth.
n.Wintermark: One of the three lost Silverlark songs appears to adapt a Wintermark original, and scops and other Wintermark songsmiths are invited to set its lyrics to music.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene describes travellers on pilgrimage to Bastion passing through a crossroads inn.
t.Karsk: The Charnel Lord's minions, mortal and otherwise, are sometimes encountered in the hills of Karsk, and the sovereign sleeping in its barrow there promised a gift to the new Empress.
t.Morrow: The stargazer Cassius had been given refuge in a spire in Morrow before abruptly leaving it after the Autumn Equinox to walk to Anvil.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the opening scene notes travellers journeying down the coast to the Necropolis.
t.Otkodov: The Thule merchants of the Five Fang Consortium sought Imperial investment for an unspecified scheme in Otkodov.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but linked through Cassius, a refugee from the Arch of the Sky, a spire that fell to the Druj.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but linked through Cassius, a refugee from the Arch of the Sky, a spire that fell to the Druj.

r.Karsk/Branoc: The Charnel Lord, sleeping in its well-guarded barrow in the hills of Branoc, declared its welcome for a Varushkan Empress and promised her a gift of unknown nature and timing.
r.Necropolis/Fishguard: Mentioned in passing: the Axou theologian Theodosia of Ipotavo rented a small house on the outskirts of Myfanwy's Rest and welcomed missives from Imperial scholars there.

Knocking on every door.d: Irada von Temeschwar's statement passed 250-0 at the Autumn Equinox 385YE. Any such site would swell Vigilance congregations for a year. It would let the Vigilance assembly send the vigilant into a named territory to root out threats, at the cost of disruption there. It would also make people less inclined to rely on magistrates, and would strengthen aspirationalism. Three General Assembly mandates were prepared. The first is his fire-damaged basilica in Bastion, which needs restoring and focuses on Empire-wide threats. The second is his tomb in the Necropolis, focused on local threats and the young. The third is the Ringblack Shrine in Tassato Regario, focused on direct action and ringblack stories. The choice could rekindle old disputes between the Virtue assemblies.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the threat of Grendel invasion is credited with silencing old arguments over Berechiah, and a League mountebank removing someone paid by a Grendel to spy is given as an example of the vigilant acting without magistrates.
n.Highguard: Berechiah, who left the League to become Highborn, has two of the three candidate sites in Highguard: his damaged basilica in Bastion and his tomb in the Necropolis. Highborn Vigilants and the Custodes Clavium stand to play a central role in the consecration.
n.The League: Berechiah was a Tassatan orphan and bravo, and one candidate site is a Vigilance shrine in Tassato Regario. That choice is expected to have a profound influence on the League's bravos, though vigilant investigations in League cities could disrupt Businesses.

t.Bastion: Berechiah's basilica in Bastion, burned in 303YE and never repaired, is one proposed site. Restoring it would need a commission of at least 10 wains of white granite and 5 of weirwood, and could lead to a new title, the Clavem Iudicii.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: recent events in Holberg involving sword scholars, Emperor Frederick and the mandate of Erasmo di Tassato are expected to combine with ringblack novels to influence League bravos if the Tassato Regario shrine is chosen.
t.Necropolis: Berechiah's little-known tomb, built under the name Bertolli di Tassato, lies in the Necropolis and is one proposed site. Consecrating it would emphasise teaching the young and guarding against local threats, and would likely shake up the sodality of the Silent Bell.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos is not named on the page; it only notes generally that vigilant investigations in a League city could disrupt Businesses for a season.
t.Tassato: Tassato is Berechiah's birthplace, where he rose from orphan to wealthy citizen. It hosts one of the three candidate sites, the Ringblack Shrine in Tassato Regario.

r.Tassato/Enterio: Mentioned in passing: Merchant-Prince Maria Moor, who published Berechiah's works, closed her press and retired to an orange orchard in Enterio, where she still lives.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: The former Moor's Mill printworks, which published Berechiah's books, is now a shrine where bravos and mountebanks watch the neighbourhood and print "Stories of the Vigilance". Its congregation is willing to see it consecrated as an inspirational location focused on direct action.

Listen to your heart.d: Angered by Freeborn corsairs smuggling citizens out from under Governor Rahab and stealing the Scorrero Nets, the Grendel struck hard at the Brass Coast. Their raiders now menace all Imperial fleets on the Bay of Catazar. Building on Martha i Guerra's Autumn Equinox statement calling for raids on enemy shipping, a mandate could send Freeborn corsairs to hunt the Grendel. This would lift the penalty on Freeborn fleets and unlock a lucrative 'Hunt the Grendel' action, but would break the terms of the eternal Ephisis's offer. Alternatively, Beatriu i Dalila i Guerra proposed an 'Escort Imperial Shipping' mandate. This would lift the penalty for all fleets on the Bay and win allies from other nations. Only one mandate could be pursued.

n.Grendel: Grendel raiders were boarding Imperial fleets across the Bay of Catazar in revenge for Freeborn humiliations. Freeborn corsairs might be sent to slaughter their crews and plunder their ships, or to steer Imperial merchants away from them.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun raids are listed among the attacks the Freeborn had been fending off before the Grendel struck.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn Assembly could choose between taking the fight to the Grendel for plunder, at the cost of breaching the Ephisis offer, or protecting all Imperial shipping to win allies for reclaiming Madruga.

t.Bay of Catazar: Grendel fleets were seeking to dominate the Bay, penalising Imperial shipping there. Either proposed mandate would lift that penalty, for Freeborn fleets alone or for all fleets on the Bay.
t.Madruga: Madruga was described as burning under Grendel attack. Supporters of the escort mandate argued the Brass Coast could not reclaim it without allies from other nations.

Out of the abyss.d: Priests answering Marzanna's statement anointed some miners but were barred from the Deep Chamber by the cabalists of Void. The work is now complete. Missing miners and failing lights have driven demand for Urizeni lightstone, which Cold Sun is disrupting. Businesses in both nations could diversify to secure light supplies. A one-season great work offered a House of Illumination at Cargo and a Light Market in Miekarova, raising mine and business investment, creating two titles and reducing the danger to miners. The sovereign offered to trap the Cold Sun scions in the Star Caverns, asking for those caverns and Berislav's Rest mine. Varushkans were invited to negotiate through a Sentinel Gate conjunction.

n.Urizen: Urizeni businesses could diversify for free to supply lightstone northwards. The proposed House of Illumination and Architect of Illumination title would boost trade in Morrow and Redoubt and could forge closer ties with Varushka, building on Cassia Silkweaver's statement of thanks.
n.Varushka: Varushkan miners face a resurgent Night Below and dwindling supplies of good lightstone. Varushka was offered a Light Market and a Merchant-Boyar title, while its cabalists and senators were invited to bargain with the sovereign to destroy the Shepherds of Ash.

t.Karov: The Cold Sun scions' brief proximity to the Tallowman's Post in Karov drew the Night Below's attention, and disruption in Karov has endangered the supply of good lighting; Karov's cabalists are listed among those invited to the conjunction.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: two cabalists of Karsk are listed among the cabalists of Varushka who may attend the conjunction.
t.Miekarova: Miekarova's miners are among those most threatened by the Night Below, and the proposed great work would establish a Light Market there and raise mine investment in the territory to 2.
t.Morrow: As a centre of Urizeni lightstone production, Morrow's businesses would gain 1 level of investment if the House of Illumination great work were completed.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: six cabalists of Ossium are listed among the cabalists of Varushka who may attend the conjunction.
t.Redoubt: The proposed House of Illumination would be built at Cargo in Redoubt, raising business investment there by 1 and becoming the charge of the Architect of Illumination.
t.Volodmartz: Cold Sun's presence is disrupting lightstone imports to Volodmartz. Its senator must consent if the sovereign is to take the Star Caverns, and the sovereign also demands the mine at Berislav's Rest in return for destroying the Shepherds of Ash.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen Assembly's statement thanks the Varushkan boyars for donating an Imperial Wayleave so the Gardens of Pallas could be built in Zenith.

r.Miekarova/Dupadealuri: The proposed Light Market would be established at the walled town in Dupadealuri, receiving Urizeni lightstone carried north along the Blood Red Roads.
r.Volodmartz/Brez: The Deep Chamber was completed in the darkness beneath the Mountains of Brez, where the Night Below has its places of power. Under the sovereign's plan, Brez must be left unwarded so the Shepherds of Ash are drawn towards its people.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: The Shepherds of Ash are currently penned in at Livardz by the Varushkan covens, and the sovereign's plan would draw them out towards Murupa.
r.Volodmartz/Murupa: The sovereign wants to trap the scions in the Star Caverns in northern Murupa and then claim the caverns. Murupa must be left unwarded as bait, and the conjunction opens on the nearby Varyu Mets woodland.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: The sovereign's plan calls for ice citadels to be raised in Opascari to wall off the Shepherds of Ash and funnel them towards Murupa.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: The sovereign's plan calls for wards of living wood to be woven in Suvretz, helping channel the Shepherds of Ash towards the Star Caverns.

Part of this together.d: Lady Clarice Novarion's change of doctrine passed the General Assembly 3013-159, and the Assembly of Nine endorsed it. Priests spent personal liao promoting it, and three effects followed. Pride in the Empire surged, making virtue-focused statements of principle likelier to produce mandates for a year. Interest in the Assembly of the Way revived: priests preaching the Way gain two extra Synod votes until Autumn 386YE, and that Assembly's greater-majority statements carry General Assembly weight this summit. Acceptance of orcs also increased. Abroad, the Sumaah will urge retention of the old doctrine, while the Commonwealth and the Sarcophan approve. Mandates to spread the new doctrine to the Delves and Asavea are possible.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Lady Clarice Novarion proposed the change and was widely praised for the poetic, inspiring prose of the new Doctrine.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj were thought very unlikely to care one way or the other about the change.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel somehow learned of the change and responded smugly, as they do to everything.
n.Highguard: The new Doctrine satisfied Highborn guardians seeking words to fortify the soul. The Highborn Assembly is one of the bodies that could mandate missionaries to carry it to Asavea's hidden pilgrims.
n.Imperial Orcs: The doctrine affirms that orcs share in virtue as equals. Credit for the change was given to the Imperial Orcs' example and their armies' service in every nation, and their priests Bonewall Rek and Bonewall Cole were credited with the earlier groundwork.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun were thought very unlikely to care one way or the other about the change.
n.Navarr: The change nurtures the growing relationships between the Navarr and the Great Forest Orc steadings settling in Therunin, Hercynia and Miaren.
n.The Marches: The change makes it impossible not to recognise the Mournwold Orcs as fellow Marchers. Its words also gave Marcher friars a rousing sermon for the muddy fields.
n.Urizen: Urizen questors found the new Doctrine able to withstand the intellectual rigour they demand.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: a proposed mandate urges pilgrims in Sarcophan to follow Bastion's lead in embracing the change.
t.Hercynia: Relations with the Great Forest Orc steadings in Hercynia are strengthened by the new acceptance of orcs.
t.Miaren: The change nurtures growing relationships with the Great Forest Orc steadings in Miaren.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold Orcs there gain wider acceptance, now unmistakably recognised as fellow Marchers.
t.Therunin: The change eases relations with the Great Forest Orc steadings in Therunin.

Pride of the Marches.d: Using a Boon of Finding, Kimus' heralds traced the vorpal sword with which Tom Drake slew the tyrant-boyar Alderei the Fair. It is not an artefact, but it is the lawful heirloom of William Drake, a retired yeoman of Redstone. It was last wielded against the Jotun in the Mournwold in 349YE. William distrusts the Conclave. He will release the blade as regalia of the General of the Drakes only if two conditions are met. First, Tom Drake must be researched and published or recognised by the Synod as an exemplar of Pride.
