Second, the Senate must reinstate Drake's Due, adding 5 Thrones to the Drakes' upkeep each season. That would restore the Drummers and give the army the Pride of the Marches quality.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the sword was last wielded in battle against the Jotun in the Mournwold in 349YE, before that territory was lost.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Drummers' recruitment in other nations is contrasted with how the Navarr help those already seeking a new place in the Empire.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the opening story shows a carta of mountebanks trying to pass off a battered shield as Tom Drake's relic to hopeful Marchers.
n.The Marches: The Marches have a chance to recover their founding general's sword for the Drakes. They could also see Tom Drake honoured as an exemplar of Pride and the Drummers revived, if the Senate restores Drake's Due and the historical research or Synod recognition goes ahead.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the sword is the blade that killed the Varushkan tyrant-boyar Alderei the Fair in the battle that also cost Tom Drake his life.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: the fake relic in the opening story was a real Marcher shield recovered from a battlefield outside Holberg.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold is named as one of the territories where the Drakes' billet order is already available.
t.Mournwold: The sword was last used in the final fight against the Jotun here in 349YE. If Drake's Due is reinstated, the billet order would also become available in the Mournwold.
t.Upwold: Tom Drake's vorpal sword was found in Upwold, at William Drake's home on the family farmland in Redstone, where Tom Drake lies buried in Tom's Orchard.

r.Upwold/The Heath: The region is tied to the discovery of Tom Drake's vorpal sword in Upwold, where his descendant William Drake keeps it above the hearth and refuses to let visitors trespass to see it.

Prospecting in Skarsind.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by Spiral, the motion took up the opportunity from the Standing in the Sun Wind of Fortune. With support from the Order of the Golden Pyramid, encouraged by the Imperial Conclave, the cost fell to 100 thrones, which Irontide Flax provided after the Winter Solstice; the work takes three months. Once complete, upgrading Imperial Orc military units costs one wain less mithril (minimum one wain), and Imperial Orc armies in Skarsind gain the Forge Hammers order: camping around the Black Forge above Gildenheim, suffering a fifth more casualties but defending three tenths better, with extra strength from mithril used for emergency resupply.

n.Imperial Orcs: Imperial Orc armies gain cheaper upgrades, needing one wain less mithril, and access to the Forge Hammers order to defend Skarsind from the Black Forge.

t.Skarsind: Human miners come to work the Imperial Orc mines in Skarsind's northern hills, and the Black Forge above Gildenheim becomes a fortified camp from which orc armies can defend the territory.

Ripples and shadows.d: After Imperial armies withdrew from Sanath, curses of walking trees and blight struck the Salt Flats, and the Druj blamed the Empire. The Golden Sun crushed the Druj in Murderdale and swept the Barrens, making every region except the Heart of Peytaht Imperial and Dawnish. The Spears of the Pines and the Navarr Quiet Step took the Heart of Peytaht and its weirwood grove. The Northern Eagle killed every defender of Dourfell Keep, though warned survivors escaped to Peytaht. The Iron Helms executed Black Wind leaders and took hostages to force the sept's army home. The Karass all but annihilated the Vendarri. Every act was lawful against Senate-declared barbarians.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun annihilated the Druj in Murderdale and secured the Barrens, so every region except the Heart of Peytaht is now Imperial and part of Dawn.
n.Druj: The Druj were driven entirely from the Barrens and only around a hundred escaped. In the Salt Flats they turned the lingering curses into propaganda against the Imperial humans.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc Assembly sent Skywise Rykana with food and supplies to the Rahvin in Bitter Strand, and the Rahvin keep control of the Fangs mithril mine.
n.Navarr: Almost five thousand Navarr of the Quiet Step, supported by a liao-backed assembly mandate, fought beside the Great Forest Orcs to retake the Heart of Peytaht. They were embraced as siblings of the spirit.
n.Varushka: The Northern Eagle destroyed the Montanians at Dourfell Keep and burned their writings. The Iron Helms executed Black Wind leaders and took hostages to compel the sept's army to return.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the only Synod statement of principle against the Barrens actions to pass with a greater majority came from the Wintermark assembly.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Golden Sun came to the Barrens fresh from their furlough in Astolat.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: some fleeing Druj escaped west into Brocéliande, where they will be hunted by humans and orcs alike.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: After the Imperial invasion withdrew, walking trees, chill weather and herb blight ravaged the territory. The Druj blamed the curses on the Empire to cow the people.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride left the Barrens and passed west into Semmerholm.
t.The Barrens: The territory is now almost wholly Dawnish and free of the Druj, but its septs are in shock. The Montanians are destroyed, the Black Wind are subjugated and the Vendarri are wiped out, while Druj curses on the trees fade towards Spring.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs and the Montanians returned from exile in Therunin, and some Montanians chose to stay there.

r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens: The Iron Helms and other Imperial armies withdrew from the Fens back into the Barrens, leaving the region beset by curses that the Druj blamed on the Empire.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: The Rahvin there received Imperial Orc aid, and a few isolated Vendarri settlements near Bitter Strand escaped the Karass massacre.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Great Forest Orcs and Navarr defeated the Druj at the weirwood grove and now control the region. The surviving Montanian refugees have found sanctuary there.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Northern Eagle killed every defender of the Montanian council at the ruins of Dourfell Keep and burned the bodies and books. A few hundred non-combatants had already fled west.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: The Golden Sun crushed the reeling Druj forces here. The Iron Helms later executed the leaders of the region's Black Wind villages and took hostages.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The Karass made a surprise attack and slaughtered hundreds of Vendarri, destroying their settlements and effectively ending the sept as a force in the Barrens.

Road out of nowhere.d: Graciana proposed extending roads to Mitwold, Mournwold, Skarsind, Sermersuaq, Weirwater and Hercynia; this later expired after tolls were levied on the Blood Red and White Roads. Marshways for Kallavesa, Therunin and Bregasland, each with a new title, were superseded by The circle game. In Zenith, white granite was found at the ruined Arch of the Sky; a mithril skyway could create a Bourse seat yielding 18 wains a season and be extended across Urizen and Spiral. A road could link Drycastle in the Barrens to Lacre and Holberg. The Navarr Assembly could create Roadwardens. Completed networks would raise taxation. Armies or invaders could threaten construction, and offers ran until Spring 388YE.

n.Dawn: A proposed road from Drycastle to Lacre and Holberg would help rebuild Dawnguard, raise farm and business investment in the Barrens, and let Dawnish citizens take a new Barrens resource free for a year; Weirwater was also among the expired highway proposals.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having destroyed the Arch of the Sky in 381YE and as having long occupied and wrecked Dawnguard.
n.Highguard: The tolls on Highguard's White Roads helped end the highway opportunity, and the proposed skyway would deliver white granite via Cargo across the river to Bastion.
n.Imperial Orcs: Skarsind was one of six territories that could have gained a road network raising farm and business investment, an opportunity that later expired.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: a carter in the fiction grumbles about constant Jotun invasions of the Marches, and Jotun-held Bregasland featured in the since-superseded marshways proposal.
n.Navarr: A greater-majority Navarr Assembly statement could have wayhouses support roadwardens, creating a Roadwardens opportunity for Navarr military units; Hercynia was offered roads and Therunin marshways.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Sunset Roads are cited as an existing network, and the kamkrag in Kahraman inspired the roadwarden idea.
n.The League: A road from Holmauer's southern gates would link Holberg to Drycastle, Spiral could join the Urizeni skyway, and Tassato's washing lines helped inspire the idea.
n.The Marches: Mitwold and Mournwold were offered roads to raise farm and business investment, though the opportunity later expired; the opening fiction mocks the poor state of Marcher tracks.
n.Urizen: White granite was found at the ruined Arch of the Sky, and a mithril skyway could create a Bourse seat and be extended to boost mana site and business investment across Morrow, Zenith and Redoubt.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Iron Roads are cited as an existing network, Varushka's hard line on banditry is noted, and roadwardens might go there to fight wolves.
n.Wintermark: Sermersuaq was offered a road network, later expired, while Kallavesa's marshways proposal, with a Shadow of the Marsh title at Rundahl, was superseded.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: the proposed skyway would end at Cargo, with white granite carried across the river to Bastion.
t.Bregasland: Judged too marshy for roads, Bregasland was offered marshways and a Bregas Ferrymaster title based at Ottery, a proposal later superseded by The circle game.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia was one of six territories that could have gained a road network raising farm and business investment, an opportunity that later expired.
t.Holberg: A sturdy road from Holmauer's southern gates to Drycastle was proposed as one of two routes linking the Barrens to the Empire.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the kamkrag being built there inspired the roadwarden idea, and recent events there illustrate the risk invaders pose to construction.
t.Kallavesa: Too wet for roads, Kallavesa was offered marshways and a Shadow of the Marsh title with offices at Rundahl, a proposal later superseded by The circle game.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov is not named; the page refers only generally to Varushka's Iron Roads and its stance on bandits.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is not named; the page refers only generally to the Brass Coast's Sunset Roads.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold was offered a road network raising farm and business investment by one, an opportunity that later expired after tolls were levied.
t.Morrow: Too mountainous for roads, Morrow would host the proposed skyway carrying white granite through Caeli and Operus, with an extension raising mana site and business investment.
t.Mournwold: Mournwold was offered a road network raising farm and business investment by one, an opportunity that later expired after tolls were levied.
t.Redoubt: Too mountainous for roads, Redoubt could be linked by an extended skyway that would raise its mana site and business investment by one.
t.Semmerholm: Lacre would be linked to Drycastle by a proposed highway through Axmure, part of the Barrens road plan.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was offered a road network raising farm and business investment by one, an opportunity that later expired.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind was offered a road network raising farm and business investment by one, an opportunity that later expired.
t.Spiral: Too mountainous for roads, Spiral could join the skyway, raising business investment, though its mana sites would only benefit if the Senate stopped funding mana for the Urizen there.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: its washing lines strung between houses partly inspired the skyway design.
t.The Barrens: A proposed road linking Drycastle to Semmerholm and Holberg would aid Dawnguard's rebuilding, raise farm and business investment, and let Dawnish citizens take a new resource there free for a year.
t.Therunin: Too vallorn-ridden and marshy for roads, Therunin was offered marshways and a Brand of the Fens title, later superseded; Graciana also proposed the roadwardens idea there.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater was offered a road network raising farm and business investment by one, an opportunity that later expired.
t.Zenith: White granite was found at the ruined Arch of the Sky on the Starstair; quarrying it via a skyway would mean the spires could never be rebuilt, and an extension would boost mana site and business investment.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: A sturdy road would run from Holmauer's southern gates to Drycastle in the Barrens.
r.Morrow/Caeli: The proposed Bridge of the Air would stretch mithril cables from the Starstair to the lower peaks of Caeli.
r.Morrow/Operus: The skyway would be extended through Operus, past Canterspire Circle, to reach Cargo.
r.Semmerholm/Axmure: A highway through the forests of Axmure would link Lacre with Drycastle.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: a road from Drycastle through Murderdale to the Eaves of Peytaht is floated as a possible future extension.

Standing in the sun.d: After Ashborn Atla accepted Highborn aid, priests and experts visited Skarsind. The Senate paid 100 thrones, with Golden Pyramid support, to bring miners to Skarsind. Orc units now upgrade for one fewer wain of mithril, and an army can defend the Black Forge with improved resupply. General, Highborn and Varushkan Assembly mandates opened a Bone Pilgrimage for orc and Highborn units everywhere except Urizen. The Senate declined to outlaw exorcising orc ghosts. The Feldspar Distillery and Wise Arborist were created, but realmsroot secrets were not shared with Highguard. An amended Legion Engineer let the Tamazi wall Gildenheim, completed shortly before Autumn 387YE. The Sannite fighting pit was not built, and the Ambition Assembly pursued a memorial to Thrace.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: as the former masters who denied the Ethengraw their own weapons, from whom the Illarawm hid their ancestors' bones, and whose auras the Yerende knew in Ossium.
n.Highguard: Highborn priests, gardeners and engineers offered peerless kinship to the orc septs and consecrated Loyalty and Prosperity auras in the Palace of Flowers. Highborn military units may now join the Bone Pilgrimage, though the orcs chose not to share herbsheart with High Chalcis.
n.Imperial Orcs: The septs gained cheaper unit upgrades from the Black Forge, a Wise Arborist teaching realmsroot cultivation, walls around Gildenheim and the Bone Pilgrimage to bring their ancestors home. Their plea to outlaw exorcism of orc ghosts and the Sannite fighting pit both went unanswered.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Tamazi who had seen the walls of Temeschwar and Holberg were spurred to want Gildenheim fortified.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: as the breakers of Gildenheim's old walls, holders of a fortification at Crow's Ridge and builders of old mine-workings in Skarsind.
n.Urizen: Because the General Assembly mandate lacked a greater majority, Urizen remains the one Imperial nation where orcs seeking their ancestors' bones are not welcome.
n.Varushka: The Varushkan Assembly sent Yevanshka to urge Varushkans to support the Bone Pilgrimage, so orcs seeking Sunstorm ancestors in the vales are welcomed. Varushkan units may face any dark forces this stirs through the Adventure in Varushka.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Highborn likened a possible memorial to Thrace to Atuman's tomb on the cliffs overlooking the bay.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, but linked through the Highborn comparison with Atuman's tomb.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Tamazi who had visited Holberg were inspired to want walls for Gildenheim, and its walls inspired Ketus Stonewalk's impractical first plan.
t.Necropolis: The Highborn Assembly's support for the Bone Pilgrimage widened the stewards of the dead's calling, offering occasional chances to recover Imperial heroes and bring them back to the Necropolis.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: as the old home from which the Illarawm carried their ancestors' bones and the Yerende came to Skarsind.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: as the land whose potential aggression the Will in Skogei Glens was built to guard against.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: not named, but as Urizen land it lies outside the Bone Pilgrimage's welcome.
t.Reikos: A mandate could have had the Yerende supply herbsheart to the Gardens of High Chalcis, adding realmsroot to Reikos herb gardens, but the Imperial Orcs did not pass it.
t.Skarsind: The territory gained new miners and prospectors, Black Forge resupply for defending armies, the Ossuary Temple as the Bone Pilgrimage's destination, the Feldspar Distillery in Solvihill and new walls around Gildenheim.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: its walls galvanised the Tamazi and set the standard the Walls of Gildenheim were meant to rival.

r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Mentioned in passing: as the site of the Thule fortification built from the ruins of the old Crow's Keep.
r.Skarsind/Estermark: Mentioned in passing: as the forested hills where many Sannite live and where a Sannite folly might one day be built.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Gildenheim was fortified with Tamazi labour by Autumn 387YE, and the Black Forge in the hills above the city now offers improved resupply to a defending army. A proposed fighting pit near the Legion's Rookery was not built.
r.Skarsind/Skogei Glens: Mentioned in passing: as home to the Will, the Winterfolk-built castle facing Otkodov.
r.Skarsind/Solvihill: The Yerende Palace of Flowers received Highborn consecrations of Loyalty and Prosperity, and the Feldspar Distillery was built there to train orc herbalists to grow realmsroot under the Wise Arborist.

The best soil.d: Mel Bleak's mandate sent Sister Meredith and the egregore Jack to welcome the orcs, with 'paperwork later'. Almost all orcs seeking to bond with the egregores succeed, though integration will take time. The orcs reject the Doctrines of the Howling Abyss and question the Ancestors, so they remain heretics. A strong Synod denunciation could bring bloodshed on them from their neighbours. The Marcher and Imperial Orc assemblies were offered mandates pledging to defend them, and Highguard an alternative sending grey pilgrims to challenge them. Shared work on the Black Canal won Marcher hearts. That Great Work still needs 20 weirwood, 22 white granite and 3 crowns. The Marches could now raise a fifth army.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Doctrine of Enlightenment is said to have smoothed the transition of the Apulian orcs from being Grendel to joining the League.
n.Highguard: Aemon offered the Highborn National Assembly an alternative mandate sending grey pilgrims to persuade the Marcher Orcs that orcs do not reincarnate. The page warns the pilgrims would be forced to accept that the orcs will not give up the belief.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc assembly had already declared the Mourn Orcs to be Marchers and orc souls a matter for orcs. It could now pass a mandate sending preachers to debate the afterlife with the Marcher Orcs and pledging to defend them against any charge of heresy.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher Orcs are their former thralls, who fear what would happen if the Jotun returned. Future orc warriors might join Marcher armies to fight them.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the new doctrine removed another barrier between the Navarr and the Great Forest Orcs who established steadings in Miaren and Hercynia.
n.The Marches: The Marches began taking in the Mournwold Orcs as citizens, accepting heretics into the nation for their virtue, though some resistance remains. The nation now has the chance to raise a fifth army supported by its new orc citizens.

t.Bregasland: A few Marcher Orcs are very cautiously seeking homes here. The unsettled situation in Bregasland is also the main risk to supporting a fifth Marcher army should it slide into open rebellion.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs established steadings here, and the new doctrine eased relations with their Navarr neighbours.
t.Miaren: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs established steadings here, and the new doctrine eased relations with their Navarr neighbours.
t.Mitwold: Mournwold Orcs are studying the great farms of Mitwold and some hope to settle there. The nearly finished Black Canal would raise investment in Mitwold's farms and businesses once completed.
t.Mournwold: Most Marcher Orcs still live in the Mournwold, holding much of its best farmland and mines, and are joining the Marches there. The Black Canal would boost the territory's businesses and mines on completion.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: some Marcher Orcs are already seeking new homes and opportunities in Upwold.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: before the orcs became Marchers, fully exploiting the Mournwold's wealth would have required clearing the old woodlands at Alderly.

The greatest city in the world.d: Holberg won the competition Harlequin spread across the League with 306 wains, ahead of Sarvos (212), Temeschwar (165), Tassato (76) and Spiral (21). Three opportunities followed: excavate before Holfried's walls (500 thrones, no slot); make Holmauer an uplifting Garden City (50 thrones, four commission slots); and develop the Flaxen Pillars, a weirwood grove the Sand Fishers found in Misericorde. The Senate commissioned the Garden City, now begun, and, after a League Synod statement by Isaia Davonne di Sarvos, the Flaxen Pillars as an auctioned national League seat. Hildebrand von Holberg's judgement led to plans for the Temple of Tall Flowers, a temple-orphanage. Frederick di Sarvos's Memorial of Flowers to Lisabetta began in the Necropolis, open to donations.

n.Druj: The Sand Fishers fear the Druj will covet the Flaxen Pillars' weirwood, so the new Burgher is charged with defending the grove and Misericorde against them; their earlier siege had left Holmauer in ruins.
n.Highguard: Work began in the Necropolis, with the Cenotaph and the House of Seven Mirrors, on the Memorial of Flowers honouring Empress Lisabetta, due for completion by the Summer Solstice.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: flower cuttings for Lisabetta's memorial were brought from as far away as Segura.
n.The League: Holberg was crowned the League's greatest city, the Senate began the Holmauer Garden City and commissioned the Flaxen Pillars as an auctioned League national Bourse seat after a League Synod statement, and a temple-orphanage was planned on a Holberg priest's judgement.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: flower cuttings for Lisabetta's memorial were brought from as far away as Kallavesa.

t.Holberg: Holberg won the contest comfortably, hung a banner proclaiming its greatness, and gained plans to deepen Holfried's defences, a Garden City under way in Holmauer, the Temple of Tall Flowers, and the Flaxen Pillars weirwood seat in Misericorde.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: cuttings from Kallavesa were among the flowers arranged for Lisabetta's memorial.
t.Necropolis: Construction of the Memorial of Flowers, a gold-veined green marble wall around a lily-studded reflecting pool, began quietly in the Black City, with donations accepted until the Summer Solstice.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos came a respectable second with 212 wains, and Sarvosans were prominent elsewhere: Isaia Davonne di Sarvos's Synod statement shaped the Flaxen Pillars seat and Frederick di Sarvos designed Lisabetta's memorial.
t.Spiral: Spiral came last in the contest, investing just 21 wains in total.
t.Tassato: Tassato finished fourth in the contest with 76 wains invested.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar finished a close third with 165 wains invested, including 30 wains of weirwood.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: cold wet winds off the Semmerlak keep Misericorde damp, which is why the Sand Fishers want to kiln-dry the weirwood.

r.Holberg/Holfried: Holfried was offered a year-long, 500-throne plan to excavate bedrock before its walls, raising its fortification without increased upkeep or a commission slot; the opportunity can be taken at any time.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Senate commissioned the transformation of Holmauer into an uplifting Garden City, which has begun but needs more money and commissions to finish, and the Temple of Tall Flowers orphanage is planned at its centre.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers found the Flaxen Pillars weirwood grove here, and the Senate commissioned its development as an auctioned League Bourse seat producing 22 weirwood a season and charged with defending the region from the Druj.
r.Holberg/The Morass: Mentioned in passing: seeping groundwater from the Morass adds to Misericorde's damp, favouring kiln-drying of the weirwood.

The lake and the deep, dark woods.d: Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets kept suffering losses on the Semmerlak. The Senate's law against taking things from the water appeared to stop the lake spreading, but hoped-for port expansions would now need a Senate appraisal. Dho'uala was angered that the Imperial emissary at Surlac had refused to hand over a bargain-breaker. Suggested responses included an appraisal, historical research, questing knights, approaches to Summer heralds, or simply leaving her be. After the Summer challenge, Weirwater received its boon but Karov escaped its curse, and the Deadwood Knight stayed awake. It raised its slain foes into a warband of several dozen and, just before the Solstice, began killing Imperial citizens. Historical research might reveal a weakness.

n.Dawn: Dawnish fleets kept losing production on the lake, and Dawnish emissary Areloe Larmallevés's refusal at Surlac angered Dho'uala. Northern Weirwater now faces the Deadwood Knight's rampage, while some houses urge questing knights to defend lakeside villages.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: in the story the bandits first mistake their attackers for Druj ambushers, and destroying the Druj is cited as one of the Empire's more pressing concerns.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the 'affront of the Grendel' is listed among the concerns some argue deserve more attention than Dho'uala.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: in the story the bandits briefly think their silent attackers might be Navarr.
n.The League: Holberg's fleets continued to suffer the lake penalty, and a Holberg professor proposed that the Sand Fishers might know something useful about Dho'uala.
n.Varushka: Varushkan fleets kept losing production on the Semmerlak, and some lakeshore Varushkans opposed probing the sovereign's secrets. Meanwhile the Schlacta of Rot began preying on south-eastern Karov.

t.Holberg: Holberg's fleets on the Semmerlak continued to lose crew and cargo to Dho'uala, and one of its professors proposed approaching the Sand Fishers for knowledge of the sovereign.
t.Karov: Karov escaped the curse that normally follows the Deadwood Knight's challenge, but the creature is now killing in south-eastern Karov. Karov's Senator also withdrew, without discussion, a motion on the fate of criminals due for execution around the lake.
t.Karsk: People along Karsk's lakeshore are among the Varushkans who fear an appraisal would anger Dho'uala, and who will only cooperate with Lutomysla Niegoslava.
t.Ossium: Ossium's new port of Kostjyas Respite remained unmolested by Dho'uala, and its lakeshore folk share Varushkan wariness about probing the sovereign's secrets.
t.Semmerholm: Dawnish voices urged Semmerholm's senator, alongside Weirwater's, to call for champions to protect lakeside villages and vessels from Dho'uala's servants.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Nameless River is described as flowing east from the Semmerlak along the Barrens.
t.The Semmerlak: Disappearances of crew, cargo and boats continued, and Dho'uala vowed to keep taking her tithe. The waters stopped spreading, but port expansion stalled and would now need a Senate appraisal.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater received a boon after the Summer challenge, but the Deadwood Knight has since rampaged through its northern woods, killing bandits and then Imperial citizens. Surlac was where Dho'uala's emissary met the Empire.

r.Holberg/Misericorde: A Holberg professor proposed that the Sand Fisher orcs of Misericorde might know something useful about Dho'uala, though any approach to them would need careful handling.
r.Karov/Duzekani: The Deadwood Knight has avoided Duzekani, apparently unwilling to face the scions of Cold Sun there.
r.Weirwater/Hawksmoor: Shortly before the Winter Solstice the Deadwood Knight slaughtered a band of refugees fleeing south from Cold Sun, north of Hawksmoor.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: Wickmoor was the site of the Summer Solstice meeting where the Knight's ban may have been broken, and shortly before Winter the warband slaughtered a merchant caravan there.

Things that burn.d: Wintermark warbands and heralds of Cathan Canae won at Valashal and saved the Sovevann, but both Day armies remain in Hahnmark and Kallavesa. In Varushka the Shepherds of Ash ruined Livardz, while the Blade of Skies burned vales across Karov and now threatens Delev. A pulse of Day magic destroyed the trods of Volodmartz, Karov and Miaren. The Black Thorns drove the Still Walkers out of Hercynia, but the Empty Hands are petrifying Oakways. The Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains halved the Fire Beacon in Segura. Marcher armies destroyed the Ending Tide and the Still Rock. The Granite Pillar contained the Winnowers at the White Tower in Bastion. Six Sentinel Gate opportunities were announced.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights-errant died defending Bulgakov in Karov, Dawnish captains fought in Segura and in large numbers beside the Granite Pillar in Bastion, and a band of the Empty Hands has crossed into Astolat towards the Castle of Thorns.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the White Tower in Bastion, now seized by Cold Sun, was destroyed by the Druj some fifteen years earlier.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Feroz, which Grendel holds, appears only as the home territory of two Freeborn captains serving with the Burning Falcon.
n.Highguard: The Winnowers seized the White Tower and Oath-heart, the Shield of Loyalty, and spread a famine-wind through Sybella Cross, but the Granite Pillar and independent captains contained them at a cost of three hundred soldiers.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Worth in Skarsind were saved at the Autumn Equinox, and scions were seen to flee the Weeping Stone near the Skarsind border.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Bounders' general referred to traitors left behind by Fisher and the Jotun, and Jotun-held Liathaven is listed as home to some Navarr captains.
n.Navarr: The Black Thorns drove the Still Walkers from Hercynia at a cost of nearly three hundred thorns, but the trods of Hercynia, Volodmartz, Karov and Miaren were destroyed, vates were burned, and the Empty Hands devastated Miaren and destroyed First Voice Glade.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire Beacon burned its way across Segura towards Sunsong Ranch until the Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains destroyed about half of it, though it remains in Burnish.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar merchants trade at Delev, now threatened by the Blade of Skies, and a Tassato captain fought in Bastion.
n.The Marches: The Bounders, Drakes and Strong Reeds, with Isaella's Dance and Marcher captains, encircled and destroyed the Ending Tide in Gravenmarch before it could grow, and the Still Rock imploded.
n.Thule: A Thule army waited at the Sungold Pass for a signal that never came and withdrew, while Thule war-wizards with bear-wolves fought beside the Fist of the Mountains against the Fire Beacon in Segura.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: scions bound for the hot springs of Peregro were intercepted at the Equinox, and Urizen captains from Morrow and Redoubt fought in Segura and Bastion.
n.Varushka: The Shepherds of Ash left Livardz in ruins and the Blade of Skies razed vales across southern Karov, killing hundreds, cutting northern trade ministries and now threatening Delev, while every trod in Volodmartz and Karov was destroyed.
n.Wintermark: Winterfolk warbands won the Battle of Valashal with the heralds of Cathan Canae and saved the Sovevann from the Exigent Span, yet both Day armies remain in Wintermark and hundreds of Winterfolk have died.

t.Astolat: A band of the Empty Hands has crossed into Astolat heading for the rose garden of the Castle of Thorns, an opportunity for the Knight-protector of Autumn to stop them through the Sentinel Gate.
t.Bastion: The Winnowers built a fortress at the White Tower and spread a withering famine-wind, but the Granite Pillar contained them there; their presence stops herb imports from the Sarcophan Delves.
t.Bregasland: The Ending Tide gathered at the Still Rock in Gravenmarch and was destroyed by Marcher armies and Isaella's Dance, though the Keeper of the Dour Fens lost this season's mana and the sinecure's yield has changed.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: three Navarr captains from Brocéliande marched with the Black Thorns in Hercynia.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Granite Pillar marched into Bastion from Casinea, and several Casinea captains fought beside it.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: two Freeborn captains from Feroz fought with the Burning Falcon in Segura.
t.Hahnmark: The Silence Arc burned halls across Valasmark and southern Kronemark before being defeated at Valashal, but it remains in Kronemark and a splinter force threatens New Dunhall.
t.Hercynia: The Still Walkers burned Northpines and Summersend until the Wooden Fastness and the Black Thorns forced them to flee the territory, but its trods remain severed.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Fire Beacon was driven back towards the Kahraman borders, and Kahraman captains fought in the Burning Falcon.
t.Kallavesa: The Exigent Span tried to burn the Sovevann and the resting dead, but Night wards and warbands killed its grand archon and broke its beacon, driving it north into Skymark.
t.Karov: The Blade of Skies razed Bulgakov, Olvanshka and many other vales in Duzekani and Kamienczka, killing hundreds, reducing the territory's prosperity and now threatening Delev, while all trods here were destroyed.
t.Karsk: The vale of Veresk was defended at the Equinox, but scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash raided western Nitrost.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Navarr captains from Liathaven fought with the Black Thorns and the Burning Falcon.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: the Black Thorns marched north from Madruga, and Madruga captains fought with the Burning Falcon and in Bastion.
t.Miaren: The Empty Hands are almost a third of the way to conquering Oakways, petrifying the land, burning steadings across Miaren and destroying First Voice Glade and every trod in the territory.
t.Miekarova: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into eastern Dupadealuri, slaughtering merchants and pilgrims and burning farms.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: southern Mitwold would have been assaulted had the Ending Tide reached full strength, and Mitwold captains fought in Bregasland.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: scions moving on the hot springs of Peregro were intercepted at the Equinox, and a Morrow captain fought with the Burning Falcon.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: northern Mournwold might have been attacked had the Ending Tide grown, and Mournwold captains fought in Segura and Bregasland.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: many Necropolis captains fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: a Thule army waited at the Sungold Pass on the Otkodov border before withdrawing, and a captain from Otkodov fought with the Fist of the Mountains.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: a Redoubt captain fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the White Tower once watched the trods into Reikos, and many Reikos captains fought in Bastion.
t.Segura: The Fire Beacon burned settlements on the plains until the Burning Falcon and Fist of the Mountains saved Sunsong Ranch and destroyed about half of it, though it remains in Burnish.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm captains fought with the Burning Falcon and in Bastion.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: captains from Sermersuaq joined the defence of Valashal and of the Sovevann.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Halls of Worth were preserved at the Equinox, and scions fled from the Weeping Stone near the Skarsind border.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: a Tassato captain fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar merchants trade at Delev, a vale some think could one day rival Temeschwar.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: captains from the Barrens fought alongside the Granite Pillar in Bastion.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: an earlier attack on Therunin was driven off, and Therunin captains fought in Hercynia and Bastion.
t.Upwold: A breakaway force of the Empty Hands is raiding towards the Sutton Stone Quarries on the Heath, an opportunity for the quarries' holder to stop them through the Sentinel Gate.
t.Volodmartz: The Shepherds of Ash razed nearly a dozen vales in Livardz, killing hundreds and reducing the territory's taxes, while wards held them away from the rest of Volodmartz and all its trods were destroyed.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Bulgakov lay on the road into Weirwater, and Weirwater captains fought in Segura and Bastion.

r.Bastion/Stoneside: The Winnowers launched attacks into Stoneside, but the Granite Pillar's stand kept their famine-wind confined to Sybella Cross.
r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: The Winnowers seized the White Tower, raised a fortress there and blighted herb gardens, and the Granite Pillar fought them to a standstill; the Champion of Loyalty may seek Oath-heart via Tamar's Stand.
r.Bastion/Woodbury: The Winnowers erupted from a ring of magister statues in eastern Woodbury and later launched attacks back into the region.
r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: The Ending Tide gathered at the Still Rock and was destroyed when the Marcher armies closed on it; the Rock imploded and the menhirs now weep a rainbow-coloured liquid.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: The Dripping Echoes of the Fen ward was raised over the Grey Fens, its mists slowing the scions across Bregasland but also confusing Marchers and magistrates.
r.Bregasland/The Rushes: Mentioned in passing: in a world where the Ending Tide grew unchecked, it would have spilled west into the Rushes and taken Sallow.
r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: Halls on the southern downs of Kronemark burned, and the defeated Silence Arc has now been driven into Kronemark, forcing people to flee north.
r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: The Silence Arc emerged at the Lantern Gate and burned halls until defeated at Valashal by Winterfolk and a Frozen Citadel, at the cost of two hundred defenders.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: A splinter of the Silence Arc is moving east through Wood Heath to threaten New Dunhall and the keystone of the Legacy of Vigilance.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: The vallorn in Deer's Folly remains cut off from the trods, which can only be restored from a Spring regio inside the vallorn itself.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: The Still Walkers emerged from the eternal flame's cavern and burned the pines until the Wooden Fastness drove them to vanish from the region.
r.Hercynia/Old Ranging: Mentioned in passing: the Still Walkers retreated west towards Old Ranging before being trapped.
r.Hercynia/Summersend: The Still Walkers reappeared here threatening the Heartwood and the Great Library of Hacynian, but the Black Thorns killed nearly a third of them before they fled.
r.Kallavesa/Kallavesa Marsh: A Night ward shrouded the marsh against the scions, and an Exigent Span force threatens the healers of Hufi's Glen, reachable via the Road to Masi.
r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: The Exigent Span destroyed the Swanmere and tried to purge the Sovevann, but its grand archon was slain and the army driven out after months of fighting.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: The Exigent Span retreated into Skymark, where it is regrouping with Wintermark's heroes in pursuit.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: A Night ward shrouded West Marsh, and the fishing fleet of Westerhal carried warriors to relieve Rundahl.
r.Karov/Duzekani: The Blade of Skies razed Bulgakov and other vales, left the region Sun Burned with cursed glass, drove off its bees, and now threatens Delev and the northern trade ministries.
r.Karov/Kamienczka: The Blade of Skies destroyed vales including Olvanshka, home of three warden fellowships, though scions fled the Weeping Stone.
r.Karov/Malimorzi: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into northern Malimorzi, killing travellers and burning farms.
r.Karov/Skoremujac: A Wooden Fastness was forged in Skoremujac, which the Blade of Skies avoided.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Imperial magic raised a keep of blue ice and stone in Wieliczka, which the Blade of Skies avoided.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into western Nitrost, killing merchants and pilgrims and burning farms.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: A Spring ward over Goldglades sheltered refugees, though its regio were scorched by the trod-pulse; the Spear of the Seven may confront scions here at Golden Meadow.
r.Miaren/Greenfalls: The Empty Hands launched assaults into Greenfalls, attacking steadings, stridings and wayhouses.
r.Miaren/Holtford: The Empty Hands launched assaults into Holtford, attacking steadings, stridings and wayhouses.
r.Miaren/Oakways: The Empty Hands emerged at Tomma's Well, overran steadings and are nearly a third of the way to conquering Oakways, which has become Petrified.
r.Miaren/Serenael: The Empty Hands raided Serenael without attacking Seren itself, whose walls sheltered many fleeing the scions.
r.Miekarova/Dupadealuri: Scouting parties of the Shepherds of Ash struck into eastern Dupadealuri, slaughtering travellers and burning farms.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Mentioned in passing: scions moving to unleash the hot springs of Peregro were intercepted at the Autumn Equinox.
r.Segura/Burnish: The Fire Beacon emerged from a regio in Burnish's hills and, though halved in battle, is regrouping there.
r.Upwold/The Heath: Empty Hands raiders threaten the Sutton Stone Quarries, and the Sentinel Gate will open to Sammy's Paling to stop them.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: The Shepherds of Ash emerged at the Sumisev Peegel and razed nearly a dozen vales, killing hundreds; Livardz has gained the ruins quality.
r.Volodmartz/Opascari: A black granite fortress raised on Opascari's hilltops helped shield the rest of Volodmartz from the Shepherds of Ash.
r.Volodmartz/Suvretz: Spring wards over the forests of Suvretz turned the land and its beasts against the scions, keeping the Shepherds of Ash away.

Three keys.d: Heralds who fought alongside the Bloodcloaks in Skallahn and the Golden Sun in the Barrens proposed changing their qualities to Woundbinder and Golden Juggernaut. With the Rod and Shield, they proposed walls and a sea-gate for Meade, a third Mournwold fortress at Sarcombe, an expanded Reumah's Rest guarding the Necropolis coast, a deadlier Spires of Dusk, and a Water Tower in Segura. Dawnish yeofolk offered the 'Last Hound' memorial as an alternative, and Sorin's herald offered the Black Hounds statues. After the Conclave interdicted the practice, Zakalwe made Prismatic Ink stronger for certain rituals at the Winter Solstice, except for Varushkan covens. The Senate later chose to remodel the Spires, and Lofyn Blood-cloak honed the Bloodcloaks.

n.Dawn: The Golden Sun was offered an upgrade to Golden Juggernaut with a new order honouring the Hounds of Glory. The Spires of Dusk were remodelled into a monument to the Hounds and to Dawnish rule in the Barrens.
n.Druj: The Golden Sun's campaign against the Druj in the Barrens was observed by Zakalwe's heralds. The Druj traps and the last traces of their power at the captured Spires of Dusk were torn out when the Senate chose the remodelling.
n.Grendel: The Grendel threat to the Necropolis coast prompted the proposal to raise Reumah's Rest to rank three and protect Longbeach and Sanctuary Sand from attack by sea. Their growing threat also figured in the Segura Water Tower plan.
n.Highguard: Highguard was offered a costly upgrade of Reumah's Rest in Necropolis, with sea walls, watchtowers and seabells along the whole coast to guard the tombs against the Grendel.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were the foes the Bloodcloaks fought in Skallahn. The proposed Sarcombe Pie scheme would stop them making Mournwold 'under threat' or using beachhead-easing orders there while all three fortresses stood.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Night magic that gave Navarr armies murderous fervour in Kahraman was cited as an example of the practice the Conclave interdicted.
n.The Brass Coast: Segura was offered the Water Tower fortress, with kamkrag outposts, protection from raiding and more marrowort. The Fire of the South's recent savagery enchantment was cited as the kind of magic now interdicted.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the walls of the League's cities are said to stir long-held jealousy among Meade's alders.
n.The Marches: The Marches were offered Bridget's Walk at Meade, with a new Merchant of Meade title, and the Sarcombe Pie scheme to guard Mournwold. Marcher orcs and alders offered to fund a third of the latter.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule is referenced only through the Bloodcloaks' disastrous retreat from Otkodov a century ago.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the page makes no specific reference to Urizen; it is linked only through the Empire-wide boons.
n.Varushka: Varushkan covens were singled out as the only ones Zakalwe would not let benefit from his Winter Solstice Prismatic Ink boon, and his heralds would not say why.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks could become a Woundbinder army by reviving the old scildran tradition of shield-bearers protecting grimnir. General Lofyn Blood-cloak provided the mithril and weirwood to make the change.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion is not specifically addressed; Highguard's interest here lies in Necropolis.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: its occupation was noted among recent invasions of the Marches, and the heralds asked to explore its fens.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the kamkrag proposal there inspired the Segura plan, and a Navarr campaign there was cited as an example of savagery magic.
t.Mitwold: Meade could be walled with a sea-gate as Bridget's Walk, creating a Merchant of Meade title to buy Caitun metals and swords for the market towns of Mitwold.
t.Mournwold: A new fortress at Sarcombe, backed by towers, sanctuaries and armouries, was proposed to guard the whole territory against Jotun incursions.
t.Necropolis: Reumah's Rest could be raised to a rank three fortification whose protection extended along the whole coast against seaborne Grendel attacks.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Bloodcloaks were destroyed in a retreat from Otkodov almost a century ago.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt is not specifically addressed on the page.
t.Segura: The Water Tower and kamkrag were proposed to protect all of Segura from raiders such as the Corazón and to extend irrigation to its herb gardens. The Zemress families offered half the cost if it were commissioned by the Spring Equinox 386YE.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe's heralds observed the Bloodcloaks campaigning against the Jotun there.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Temeschwar is not specifically addressed on the page.
t.The Barrens: The heralds observed the Golden Sun fighting the Druj here. Of the rival plans for the Spires of Dusk, the Senate chose to remodel it as a monument to the Hounds of Glory.

r.Mitwold/Meade March: Bridget's Walk, a rank one fortification with walls across the river mouth and a sea-gate, was proposed for Meade here.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Mentioned in passing: Alderly was named as a region where the Jotun might plant hidden caches as they did in Southmoor.
r.Mournwold/Green March: Mentioned in passing: Green March was named as vulnerable to Jotun caches and would be covered by the proposed protection.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Jarl Haakon's hidden caches had left Southmoor under threat, and the Sarcombe Pie fortress was proposed there to end that threat.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Reumah's Rest stands in Coursmouth, and the proposed upgrade would make it a rank three fortress overseeing coastal defences.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Longbeach and Crown's Quay, currently poorly protected, would be shielded by the upgraded Reumah's Rest against attacks from the sea.
r.Necropolis/Sanctuary Sand: The beaches where the first Highborn landed would be protected by the upgraded Reumah's Rest against seaborne assault.
r.Segura/Iron Plains: The Iron Plains were proposed as the central site for the Water Tower, a rank two fortification guarding the whole of Segura.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: Home to the Zemress Islanders and the Iron Qanat, whose farms the proposed Water Tower would shield from plundering raiders.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Mentioned in passing: Dawnish yeofolk cautiously returning here were among those who argued for the Last Hound memorial.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: The Spires of Dusk stand here. The Senate chose to strip out the Druj defences and remodel the fortress as a memorial to the Hounds of Glory.

Top and Bottom, Up and Down.d: Sinokenon argued that the Omnihedron should use only Day magic, and that the Empire should freeze all Senate, Synod and Conclave decisions and army movements for a year. Stargazers dismissed both ideas. More practically, it proposed that the Senate create a Conclave title, such as an 'Overseer of the Omnihedron', able to raise one declaration of endorsement each summit. If this is done, Carve the Crystal Guardian would gain a seven-rank bonus for a season. It also offered a cheaper Day college at Sunspire in Morrow, with an everturning wheel for its Dean. The Almighty Panjandrum (Night), Fleeting Beat for Sorin, and Grimcrow for Wise Rangara offered dissenting views.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Turning Mirror notes that the Lyceum is currently in Grendel hands, which narrows the Empire's opportunities for magical research.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Sunspire is described as guarding the forests of Therunin against incursions from the Spring realm.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Ragged Anne, an Ashill Landskeeper, mocks the Day eternal for answering a question about magic with more Day magic.
n.Urizen: Sinokenon calls the Urizeni theory of the Omnihedron flawed and is troubled that Anthemius Netherwatch was declared for organising the Urizen covens. It also proposes a cheaper Day college at Sunspire and warns that the Heliopticon may be pushed towards Autumn magic.
n.Varushka: Grimcrow, a herald of Wise Rangara, emerges from a regio in Varushkan Miekarova. It wanders the roads asking what the wisest course would be, and suggests pauses between rituals or abandoning the Omnihedron altogether.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: a Wintermark runesmith likens the Omnihedron to making steel, arguing that the right imperfections matter more than purity.

t.Miekarova: Grimcrow, a bundle of sticks, feathers and bones with a corvid skull, emerges from a regio here to spread Wise Rangara's counsel along the Empire's roads.
t.Morrow: Sunspire in Morrow is identified as the ideal site for a cheaper College of Day Magic for the next year, costing 45 mithril, 45 white granite, 60 weirwood and 450 crowns. The opportunity has not yet been taken up.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin's forests are watched over by Sunspire in neighbouring Morrow, which guards them against Spring incursions.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: an Ashill Landskeeper named Ragged Anne is quoted ridiculing the Turning Mirror's advice.

r.Upwold/Ashbrook: Mentioned in passing: Ragged Anne of the Ashill Landskeepers is quoted mocking the Day eternal's insistence on more Day magic.

Watercolours in the rain.d: The scions raided the Brilliant Star after the Autumn Equinox, taking mithril and killing those who could not flee, including Verax of the Seventh Mist and most of their students. Its Day light now causes blistering illness. Tempest jade wards protect workers but production falls by four wains, to 20 a season, unless the Senate adds 5 thrones of upkeep, which would raise it to 28. The bourse seat gains a ministry trading tempest jade for splinterstars. Pride Assembly mandates are proposed: drawing armies home, freeing Proud congregations to become military units, or boosting art venues. Civilian commissions may receive cheaper labour, and national assemblies may call for art monuments.

n.Dawn: Dawnish knights-errant helped defend the Brilliant Star, and the Rose Towers would gain 108 extra rings at the Spring Equinox 386YE if the Pride mandate to celebrate art is enacted. Dawn's National Assembly may also call for a monument to its art.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Spires of Dusk, a horror the Druj left behind, could be remodelled into a memorial to the Hounds of Glory at reduced cost.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the threat of a Grendel assault on the coast meant the White Fountain garrison could send only a small force to retake the mine.
n.Highguard: A Highborn cataphract dedicated to Vigilance was among the mine's defenders. Imperial armies are credited with saving the Grand Inspiration of the Way in Bastion from Cold Sun.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc National Assembly could raise a statement of principle calling on citizens to design a monument to their art and culture in a named territory.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies destroyed Cold Sun's Ending Tide in Bregasland, then held by the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr thorns fought to defend the Brilliant Star. Imperial armies are credited with protecting the Great Library of Hacynian in Hercynia.
n.The Brass Coast: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse and the Crimson Drummers of Madruga would each gain 108 extra rings if the art mandate is enacted. Imperial armies devastated Cold Sun's Fire Beacon in Segura.
n.The League: Congregations in Sarvos, Tassato and Temeschwar would each produce 36 extra rings under the art mandate, and Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato proposed an alternate Pride mandate. The League's assembly may also call for a monument.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost the Brilliant Star's benign light, Verax of the Seventh Mist and most of their students, and the chance to improve its ritual codification. Its armies would escape the draw-home mandate unless it passed by greater majority, and its assembly may call for a monument.
n.Varushka: Varushkan armies would only be affected by the draw-home Pride mandate if it passed by greater majority. Its National Assembly could also call for a monument to Varushkan art.

t.Bastion: Without the Imperial armies, the scions might have destroyed the Grand Inspiration of the Way here. Any nation that calls for its own monument can no longer pledge support to that great work.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies destroyed the Ending Tide here.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies are credited with preventing the destruction of the Great Library of Hacynian here.
t.Kahraman: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse would see larger audiences and its title would gain 108 extra rings if the Pride art mandate is enacted.
t.Madruga: The Crimson Drummers of Madruga would draw more visitors, and the title would gain 108 extra rings, if the Pride art mandate is enacted.
t.Redoubt: The scions seized and permanently tainted the Brilliant Star here, killing those unable to flee. The White Fountain garrison sent a small force that retook the mine, but too late to prevent the looting.
t.Reikos: Remodelling the Spires of Dusk, left behind by the Druj, into a memorial to the Hounds of Glory would cost 20 crowns less if a Pride statement supports it.
t.Sarvos: Each congregation here would produce 36 extra rings next season if the art mandate is enacted, as the city hosts pilgrims seeking art and culture.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies devastated Cold Sun's Fire Beacon here.
t.Tassato: Each congregation here would produce 36 extra rings under the art mandate. Astrid Fjellrevening Rezia di Tassato proposed an alternate Pride mandate.
t.Temeschwar: Each congregation here would produce 36 extra rings next season if the art mandate is enacted, as pilgrims come for art and culture.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Azure Chorus here would draw more visitors to its feasts and performances, gaining 108 rings, if the Pride art mandate passes.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: The Brilliant Star mine now glows with a harmful light, cutting output to 20 wains of mithril a season. A Senate-funded upkeep increase of 5 thrones would raise it to 28 wains, and splinterstars can be gathered from spent tempest jade wards.
